story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The board shows a crime scene disguised as a forest attack.
story.say: "This scene wants you to think animal attack first. The evidence gives you permission to doubt that."
story.ask: "The cart was staged, the wound is too clean, and the feeding happened after the killing. Knowledge or Instinct 12 confirms the wound."
story.deeper: Keep the later faction implications GM-only. The immediate story truth is enough: a person used the forest as cover.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Give basic search facts automatically, then use Knowledge, Instinct, or Finesse when players test the staging.
mechanic.say: "If your character just searches the cart, I will give the obvious facts. If you are reconstructing the scene or reading a body, that is where the dice come in."
mechanic.ask: "Cause of death is Knowledge or Instinct 12. Scent layers are Instinct 12. Staging in the wheel is Instinct 13. Rushed physical handling can use Finesse at 12."
mechanic.deeper: This board is the investigation procedure in one place: choose object, state method, answer obvious facts, roll gated facts.

perCharacterLayer.passive: The blood under the sweet-rot smell is older than the creature's feeding. Other PCs just smell that something is wrong.

discover.text: Places animal musk as recent, human blood as older, and a faint chemical-leather tang that belongs to neither.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can track which direction the creature came from versus which direction the killer left.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Varian, your nose sorts this out faster than the others. The blood here is older than the animal. Want to follow what that tells you?

perCharacterLayer.passive: The throat wound is a clean blade cut, not claws or teeth. Someone killed this man.

discover.text: Confirms a deliberate, practiced cut: an execution staged as an animal attack.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can secure the scene and keep the party calm and methodical.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Garrick, you have stood over bodies before. This one's wrong. Want to say how?

perCharacterLayer.passive: The cart was tipped from the wrong side to be a simple accident.

discover.text: Finds thorny bramble wedged in the carriage wheel and valuables stripped before the creature arrived.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can rig the cart to clear the road quickly or quietly pocket something useful from the wreck.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, this does not read like an accident to you. What do you notice?

perCharacterLayer.passive: From her height she sees the drag marks, the feeding place, and the death place are not the same spot.
perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can clear the overturned cart single-handed when the party is ready to move.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Khari, you can see the whole picture from up there. The man did not die where he is being eaten. Want to point that out?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Her attuned senses register no magic on the scene. Whatever happened here was mundane and deliberate.

discover.text: Confirms the absence of magic is notable; this killing was done the old-fashioned way by someone using the wild as cover.

perCharacterLayer.contribute: Can tell the party that the important package is not what caused this wreck to pulse with magic; there is no pulse here.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Marlowe, you would feel it if magic did this. You do not. That is worth sitting with.

sensorySummary: Visual reference for Sablewood Route Network.
Leaf-drip, insects, distant wingbeats, and animal calls that stop or resume according to pressure, not comfort.
Rain on leaves, sap, mushroom loam, wet bark, and the musk of unseen animals.
Bark is damp and ridged; mud alternates between springy moss and slick clay.
The forest is populated even when no NPC is present; silence, birds, insects, and tracks are actionable signals.

title: The Creature and Her Young
alt: The Strixwolf Mother scene art for The Logistics Incident.
caption: The Strixwolf Mother is dangerous, frightened, and probably not guilty of the murder.
gmGoal: Reveal the feeding creature by description first, then show that she is protecting pups and is not the simple monster story.
publicObjective: Deal with the creature without anyone, including the pups, getting hurt, and clear the road.
readAloud: From behind the cart steps a large creature: the body of a wolf, the face of an owl, broad feathered wings folded along its back. It lifts its head from the meal and studies you, unhurried, deciding whether you are a threat. Then, behind it, two smaller shapes stumble into view: clumsy, big-eyed, and keeping close to its legs.
gmNotes: Player-safe: wary mother animal, two pups, road blocked by a decision.
GM-only: she did not kill the driver; she is not manufactured.
gmScript: Say: "She has not attacked. She is watching you and keeping herself between you and the young. If you want the name, locals call this kind of creature a strixwolf. The important part right now is not the name. It is her posture. What signal do you give her?"
gmReadAloud: From behind the cart steps a large creature: wolf body, owl face, and broad feathered wings folded along her back.
She studies you, unhurried, deciding whether you are a threat.
Two smaller shapes stumble into view behind her, clumsy and big-eyed, keeping close to her legs.
gmChecklist: Describe before naming.
Introduce the pups before anyone commits to violence.
Frame the creature as wary and protective, not aggressive.
Hand the resolution to S01-04: Presence 10 to read and influence her.
gmPrivate: She is a natural preserve hybrid and a scavenger here, not the killer.
If the party blames or kills her, the real killer's trail goes quieter and the corporate forest-danger story gets easier to believe.
playerTakeaway: You face a wary mother animal and two pups; your posture decides whether this turns violent.
storyTakeaway: The apparent monster is a parent protecting young, and the encounter is about restraint before violence.
mechanicTakeaway: The next roll reads intent and influences reaction: Presence against Difficulty 10, with mercy and aggression branching the scene.

entities.name: Strixwolf Pup One
entities.summary: A wet-feathered strixwolf pup with oversized ears, bright frightened eyes, and paws too large for the body it has not grown into yet.
entities.role: Strixwolf pup
entities.personality: Pure startled instinct in a body it has not grown into yet. Bright frightened eyes, ears that swivel at every snapped twig, paws a size too big. It wants its mother and cannot understand why the road brought strangers instead.
entities.wants: To get back under its mother's wing without anyone deciding it is a trophy or a threat.
entities.sampleLine: A thin rising click, like a question no one answers.

entities.name: Strixwolf Pup Two
entities.summary: A crouched strixwolf pup with darker back feathers, round eyes, and a body tucked near the roots as if the forest itself might hide it.
entities.role: Strixwolf pup
entities.personality: The one that hides instead of freezing, wedged so far into the roots the forest seems to be keeping it. Darker, quieter, watching its sibling for the cue to bolt.
entities.wants: To stay hidden until the danger walks past, and never to be separated from the only family it has.
entities.sampleLine: A low wet trill, almost swallowed by the roots.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You face a wary mother animal and two pups; your posture decides whether this turns violent.
player.say: "She has not attacked. She is watching. What you do next sets the tone."
player.ask: "You could try to calm her, back the carriage off, give the pups room, put yourself between panic and harm, or ready a weapon. Each sends a different signal."
player.deeper: Ask for posture, not tactics first. Hands open, lowered weapons, soft voices, slow retreat, or protective positioning all give the next roll a clear fictional basis.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The apparent monster is a parent protecting young, and the encounter is about restraint before violence.
story.say: "This is not a monster blocking your road. This is a mother that found an easy meal, and she has young."
story.ask: "A local or Varian can name her a strixwolf. If you ask whether she killed the driver, the body clue says no: the killing wound was a blade."
story.deeper: The players can learn the name through play, but the emotional truth lands first: mother, pups, fear, space.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: The next roll reads intent and influences reaction: Presence against Difficulty 10, with mercy and aggression branching the scene.
mechanic.say: "You are about to read her, not attack her. How you carry yourself decides what she does."
mechanic.ask: "If you try to calm or read her, this is Presence, Difficulty 10. If you attack, use the combat board; she defends the pups and tries to flee, not die."
mechanic.deeper: This scene teaches that mechanics follow approach. Mercy routes to a reaction roll; aggression routes to the combat map as a recoverable failure state.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Teach duality, outcome bands, and the slider together.
gm_runtime_payload: Roll both d12s. Add the numbers and report total plus which die came up higher.
The higher die gives the tone: Hope or Fear.
Now read the slider for this total: Botch, Miss, Hit, Clean, Soar, or Crit.
If the dice match, it is a Critical. Treat it as a success beat, award the bonus, and keep the scene moving.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: First real roll: teach official 2d12 Duality plus Kyle's slider overlay without a lecture.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Fear is escalation fuel, not punishment.
gm_runtime_payload: GM Fear starts at 1 per player and caps at 12.
Default play uses official 2d12 Duality.
Spend Fear to spotlight adversaries, make stronger moves, add adversary Experience, or trigger Fear features when the scene calls for pressure.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Keep Fear visible enough for pacing while preserving player-safe fiction.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Bank and spend Hope immediately in-context.
gm_runtime_payload: Hope starts at 2 and caps at 6.
Spend Hope on class features, Help an Ally, Experiences, and Tag Team later.
This is player currency: earning it means the table can push back.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Name Hope as immediate agency, not bookkeeping.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Teach the non-lethal path before the table misses it.
gm_runtime_payload: You do not have to end this with damage.
Approaching the strixwolf without spooking her is Presence 12.
Later, Bramble Union de-escalation is Presence 15.
On success, they pull back or listen; on Fear, the scene still asks for a cost.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Frame mercy as a viable tactic, not a hidden morality quiz.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Stress is pressure with a recovery edge.
gm_runtime_payload: Mark Stress when the consequence is strain, fear, pressure, or resource cost.
When a character marks their last Stress, they become Vulnerable until they clear at least 1 Stress.
If they must mark Stress while maxed, mark HP instead.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Make pressure visible without making it feel arbitrary.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Thresholds and severity land at the first hit.
gm_runtime_payload: Compare incoming damage to the target's thresholds.
Below Minor: mark 1 HP. At or above Major: mark 2 HP. At or above Severe: mark 3 HP.
One Armor Slot can reduce the severity by one threshold.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Teach damage once, out loud, so later hits move fast.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: One rule can unlock a better roll right now.
gm_runtime_payload: Traits use the spread +2, +1, +1, 0, 0, -1 across Agility, Strength, Finesse, Instinct, Knowledge, and Presence.
If an Experience clearly applies, spend 1 Hope for +2.
Ask the player what part of their background helps before the roll lands.
spotlights.spotlight_goal: Teach character sheets through a real risky action.

spotlights.alert_subheadline: Heightened senses catch predator panic first.
gm_runtime_payload: Varian, your Ranger focus spots the non-threat posture. Want to read the creature and shape the team's action?

publicObjective: The road tightens around the wreck. The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open, claws in the mud. The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
readAloud: The road tightens around the wreck. The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open, claws in the mud. The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
gmNotes: The creature defends and flees. She does not fight to the death unless the table hard-commits to killing a fleeing mother.
Winning does not mean killing her. Winning means road cleared and no one made the world worse.
gmScript: Say: "This is not a monster hunt. This is a defensive standoff. Every turn, you can escalate by threatening her or the young, or de-escalate by creating space, lowering weapons, opening the pups' escape route, or calming her."
gmReadAloud: The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open and claws in the mud.
The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
gmChecklist: Start with disposition at wary unless the party already attacked.
Offer a mercy route every round.
Use Fear to increase pressure, not to force a kill-box.
End the fight when she flees with the young or calms enough to leave.
gmPrivate: The right outcome is that nobody dies: no PC, no pup, not the mother.
Killing her quietly strengthens the false corporate story that the forest itself is the danger.
playerTakeaway: The road tightens around the wreck. The creature plants herself between you and the young, wings half-open, claws in the mud. The cart, the ditch, and the low branches turn the bend into a narrow standoff.
storyTakeaway: The fight is a consequence of fear; the clean win is still making space for the mother and young to leave.
mechanicTakeaway: Use normal action rolls, adversary attacks, Stress, and Fear, but keep a de-escalation route available every round.

entities.name: Strixwolf Mother
entities.summary: A huge owl-wolf mother crouched around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, acting from protection rather than malice.
entities.role: False-monster moral encounter.
entities.playerDisplayCaption: a huge owl-faced wolf mother guarding her pups near the wreck
entities.personality: Not cruel and not hungry for a fight, just a cornered parent doing math no one taught her, weighing every armed stranger against two small clicking shapes under her wing. She will let you walk away. She will not let you walk closer.
entities.wants: Keep the pups fed and far from armed strangers.
entities.sampleLine: She does not speak; she lowers her wings over the pups and tracks hands, not faces.

voice: She does not speak; she lowers her wings over the pups and tracks hands, not faces.

likes_dislikes.likes: Distance, lowered weapons, tossed food, and the party giving her a clear exit.
likes_dislikes.dislikes: Hands near the pups, shouting, bright spell-flashes, and anyone stepping between her and the trees.

block2.likes: Distance, lowered weapons, tossed food, and the party giving her a clear exit.
block2.dislikes: Hands near the pups, shouting, bright spell-flashes, and anyone stepping between her and the trees.
block2.favorite_thing: The pups' soft clicking calls, which she answers with a low chest rumble.
block2.loved_ones: The two pups under her wing; they are the reason every choice matters.
block2.day_to_day: Hunts along the route edges at dawn and dusk, using wreckage only when the forest has been pushed thin.
block2.appearance: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close. Full-body reference: Full-body owl-wolf hybrid mother, talon-tipped forepaws, barred grey-brown feathering, two downy pups at her flank, protective stance, head to feet in frame.
block2.wealth_status: Wild creature under route pressure; no wealth, only territory and offspring.
block2.animal_companion: Her pups are present and should drive every reaction.
block2.physical: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.visual_read_aloud: A huge owl-wolf mother crouches around her pups, barred feathers and fur bristling, amber eyes fixed on any hand that comes too close.
block2.voice_style: No words. A rising chest-rumble, a wing mantled over the pups, eyes that track hands instead of faces. Her warnings escalate in clear, readable stages, and she would rather you leave than test the last one.
block2.body_language: Low, protective, ready to retreat if retreat becomes safer than warning.
block2.quirks: She watches boots more than eyes because boots decide distance.
block2.image_lore: The bright feathers around her throat are not ornamental; they flare when she is trying to look larger than her fear.
block2.npc_relationships: Her future relationship to the party is animal memory: mercy can become warning, distance, or aid later.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: She expects armed two-legs to rush, shout, or claim the body without noticing the pups.
block3.persuasion_levers: Empathy and calm land. Intimidation turns the scene into a fight. Presence 12 or Instinct 11 with food opens safe access.

what_moves_them.result: She stops escalating and gives the party room to investigate.
Food and distance turn the scene from fight to wary truce.

block3.combat_lever: She breaks off as soon as the pups have room to flee or the PCs clearly choose distance over dominance.

player_safe: The road is dangerous for animals too.

gm_only: A mercy outcome can soften later wilderness pressure.

ties_to_pcs: Varian can smell fear and carrion separation; Khari can protect space without escalating.

entities.name: Strixwolf Pup One
entities.summary: A wet-feathered strixwolf pup with oversized ears, bright frightened eyes, and paws too large for the body it has not grown into yet.
entities.role: Strixwolf pup
entities.personality: Pure startled instinct in a body it has not grown into yet. Bright frightened eyes, ears that swivel at every snapped twig, paws a size too big. It wants its mother and cannot understand why the road brought strangers instead.
entities.wants: To get back under its mother's wing without anyone deciding it is a trophy or a threat.
entities.sampleLine: A thin rising click, like a question no one answers.

entities.name: Strixwolf Pup Two
entities.summary: A crouched strixwolf pup with darker back feathers, round eyes, and a body tucked near the roots as if the forest itself might hide it.
entities.role: Strixwolf pup
entities.personality: The one that hides instead of freezing, wedged so far into the roots the forest seems to be keeping it. Darker, quieter, watching its sibling for the cue to bolt.
entities.wants: To stay hidden until the danger walks past, and never to be separated from the only family it has.
entities.sampleLine: A low wet trill, almost swallowed by the roots.

sensorySummary: The cart splits the road into threat lanes: pups under cover, the mother near the wreck, brush close enough for panic to become violence.
The mother growls through a birdlike rasp; pups chirr and whine under the cart; every weapon draw makes claws scrape wood.
Blood on wet dirt, frightened animal breath, torn canvas, old feed, and the sour edge of fear-sweat from the horses.
Wheel spokes snap under weight; the ditch is slick; loose harness straps can burn palms if grabbed hard.
This is a living family in a crime scene. Let the environment answer kindness, haste, and threat posture immediately.
hazards: Spilled produce creates difficult footing around the cart.
The pups are underfoot; reckless attacks risk harming them and should trigger a safety-aware check-in.
Horse panic can pull the carriage into the road if nobody steadies it.

gmDetails.title: Defensive escalation
gmDetails.body: Start wary, not hostile. Restraint moves her toward calm. Threatening her or the pups moves her toward defensive. She fights to create space, not to kill.

gmDetails.title: Creature operating stats
gmDetails.body: Tier 1 Standard creature. Difficulty 10. Attack +1. HP 3. Stress 3. Use the linked combat workspace for full encounter tools; on this slide, the important rule is protective flight at last HP or when the pups are threatened.

gmDetails.title: The pups' escape
gmDetails.body: The pups can flee through low branches and a brush gap. Opening that path de-escalates her one step.

gmDetails.title: Per-character hooks
gmDetails.body: Khari can be a living buffer. Varian can calm by scent and posture. Garrick can talk the party down. Barnacle can open an escape path. Marlowe can offer steady presence.

combatFraming: The creature starts wary, not hostile. Track disposition as calm, wary, defensive, fleeing.
Restraint de-escalates: any round where no PC threatens her or the pups moves her toward calm.
Aggression escalates: attacking, cornering, or threatening pups makes her defensive.
She flees, not dies: at last HP or when the pups are threatened, she gathers them and escapes to a branch, watching.
hiddenTruth: She did not make the kill. Killing her buries the real killer's trail and confirms the wrong story.
Let consequences land later through silence, distrust, or lost warning signs rather than a punishment speech.
transitions: Mercy or calm: she leaves with the young, the road clears, and Act 1's first beat resolves.
Combat: the encounter ends when she flees with the young, not when she dies.
After either route: return to the carriage and travel toward the next road pressure.

title: The First Action Roll - Reading the Creature
alt: The First Roll scene art for The Logistics Incident.
caption: The first meaningful roll teaches that this adventure is about judgment, not just success.
gmGoal: Teach Duality Dice through the creature reaction roll and resolve the standoff caused by S01-03.
publicObjective: Read the creature correctly and get everyone, including the young, out of this without bloodshed.
readAloud: The creature is wary of every movement you make. Let's find out how she reacts. This is your first roll: grab your two d12s, add your Presence, and tell me the total, plus which die came up higher. If you have an Experience that fits, you can spend a Hope before you roll to add it.
gmNotes: Use the exact outcome language here so the first roll feels transparent.
After resolving the roll, return to the blocked road: the creature leaves, the road clears, or the encounter moves to the combat board.
gmScript: Say: "This is our first action roll. You are trying to read and influence a living creature, so this is Presence, Difficulty 10. Roll two d12s, add Presence, then tell me your total and whether Hope or Fear is higher. Before you roll, does an Experience fit strongly enough that you want to spend a Hope on it?"
gmReadAloud: This is your first roll: two d12s plus Presence against Difficulty 10.
Tell me the total and which die is higher: Hope or Fear.
If you have a fitting Experience, you can spend a Hope before the roll to add it.
gmChecklist: Name Presence and Difficulty 10 before dice hit the table.
Offer spend-Hope-for-Experience before the roll.
Resolve both axes: success/failure and Hope/Fear.
Route success or mercy toward a cleared road; route fear-heavy escalation to MAP-COMBAT-S01-03.
gmPrivate: This is not a floating tutorial. It is the resolution of S01-03.
Keep mercy as the clean path. Combat is a consequence of fear, threat posture, or failure, not the goal.
playerTakeaway: You now know the action-roll engine: total against difficulty, then Hope or Fear colors the result.
storyTakeaway: How you read and treat a frightened animal sets the moral tone for the rest of the route.
mechanicTakeaway: Roll Presence against Difficulty 10; 10+ succeeds, Hope/Fear changes who gains momentum, and doubles are a critical success.

rollCards.title: Make the first meaningful roll matter
rollCards.roll: Make the first meaningful roll matter
rollCards.why_this_trait: This is the teaching roll: ask what the PC does, choose the trait, then show Hope/Fear.
rollCards.stakes: The table learns that the roll changes the fiction, not just pass/fail.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
official_results.success_with_hope: Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: The table learns that the roll changes the fiction, not just pass/fail. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: None.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

rollCards.hope_spin: Gain Hope. Let the Hope result make the scene more generous, clear, or player-directed when it fits the fiction.
rollCards.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. Add pressure, reveal cost, spotlight a threat, or advance a visible consequence.
gm_fear_spends: Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.
class_community_ancestry_reveals: Ask a player to narrate what Hope or Fear looks like on their face.
rollCards.duality_text: Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add the chosen trait, compare to the Difficulty, then read the higher die for Hope/Fear spin.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You now know the action-roll engine: total against difficulty, then Hope or Fear colors the result.
player.say: "That is the engine: total beats the number or it does not; the higher die tells us who the moment favors."
player.ask: "For this roll, use Presence. If you have a fitting Experience, spend a Hope before rolling to add it. Then tell me total, Hope or Fear, and whether the dice match."
player.deeper: After this, future rolls can be faster: ask intent, name trait, name difficulty, roll, read Hope/Fear, narrate consequence.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: How you read and treat a frightened animal sets the moral tone for the rest of the route.
story.say: "This first roll is not about winning. It is about what kind of crew you are when fear gives you an easy violent answer."
story.ask: "If you calm her, she clears the way with the pups. If the scene turns hostile, she defends space and tries to flee; the road still clears, but the memory of how it happened follows you."
story.deeper: Use this result to set future texture: mercy can become warning, trust, or a feather token; cruelty can become silence, guilt, or later distrust.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Roll Presence against Difficulty 10; 10+ succeeds, Hope/Fear changes who gains momentum, and doubles are a critical success.
mechanic.say: "Ten or higher succeeds. Hope higher means you also gain Hope. Fear higher means I gain Fear and add pressure. Doubles mean a critical success: success, gain Hope, and clear a Stress."
mechanic.ask: "Success with Hope: she calms and creates space. Success with Fear: she calms, but hoot-howls as if calling another. Failure with Hope: she advances but you keep a softer opening. Failure with Fear: she advances and the roller marks Stress. Critical: she approaches head-down, tail wagging, and sits."
mechanic.deeper: This cue card is the exact table script for the first roll. Read it as needed, then narrate the specific posture and branch.

title: The Fallout Investigation
alt: The Fallout Investigation scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
caption: The cart scene becomes evidence of a claim war, not a random wilderness hazard.
gmGoal: Let the party confirm the wreck was staged, find the planted bramble, and realize the ambush is closing in.
publicObjective: Work out what really happened here before you move on.
readAloud: With the creature dealt with, the wreck is yours to read. Up close, the story stops adding up. The cart was stripped clean before anything wild got to it. The driver's wounds are not all bites. And worked into one carriage wheel, where it has no business being, is a snarl of black thorn that does not match this stretch of road.
gmNotes: Deepen Act 1's clue instead of replaying it: body, cart, wheel, tracks, then watchers.
Player-safe conclusion: people staged this and marked the carriage.
gmScript: Say: "The animal part of this scene is over. Now the wreck gets stranger. The cart was stripped before anything fed here, the killing wound is too clean for teeth, and the thorn in your wheel means somebody got close to your carriage. What do you inspect first?" If they ask who did it, say: "You do not have a name. You have method: staged, local, and deliberate."
gmReadAloud: The cart was stripped clean before anything wild got to it.
The driver's wounds are not all bites.
A snarl of black thorn is worked into one carriage wheel, where it has no business being.
gmChecklist: If Act 1 already revealed the slit throat, frame this as confirmation of staging, not a repeat reveal.
Offer Group Action Roll: one leader, helpers feed evidence.
Start or tick the Closing In countdown if they linger loudly.
Do not name the faction yet.
gmPrivate: The staging points to organized people in the preserve. Do not decide the driver's killer; the README canon flag stays unresolved.
The planted bramble is the handoff into S02-02 and the ambush board.
playerTakeaway: You now know three things: the wreck was staged, the stagers know this forest, and they have already touched your carriage.
storyTakeaway: The party is the target, not a bystander; the road incident is becoming an ambush.
mechanicTakeaway: Investigation can be a Group Action Roll: one PC leads with Instinct or Knowledge while others help assemble the scene.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You now know three things: the wreck was staged, the stagers know this forest, and they have already touched your carriage.
player.say: "Staged, local, and close. That thorn in your wheel means this was aimed at you."
player.ask: "You can inspect the body, cart, wheel, tracks, or treeline. The safest next action is to choose one thread and name who watches the carriage while you do it."
player.deeper: Keep the next action concrete: body, cart, wheel, tracks, treeline, or carriage guard. The evidence should feel playable, not abstract.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The party is the target, not a bystander; the road incident is becoming an ambush.
story.say: "This was not random damage on a road. This was a message and a setup."
story.ask: "The evidence says the people who did it understand the preserve, planned the stop, and got close to your carriage before you noticed."
story.deeper: Do not reveal the self-name or motive yet. The story truth for this scene is target, method, and proximity.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Investigation can be a Group Action Roll: one PC leads with Instinct or Knowledge while others help assemble the scene.
mechanic.say: "If you want to read this as a team, choose a lead. Everyone else says what they check and rolls to help that lead build the full picture."
mechanic.ask: "Use Instinct if you are reading tracks, smell, spacing, and threat posture. Use Knowledge if you are reconstructing wounds, staging, and procedure. Difficulty 12 for the body; 13 for the planted thorn trail."
mechanic.deeper: Group Action keeps this from becoming five separate rolls. It turns scattered observations into one shared conclusion before the ambush pressure arrives.

title: Eyes in the Brush
alt: Eyes in the Brush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
caption: Eyes in the brush turn investigation into an impending tactical decision.
gmGoal: Run the ambush spot check and fold in the strixwolf carryover before the road breaks open.
publicObjective: Notice the threat before it reaches you.
readAloud: The road feels watched. A branch snaps where no wind moved it. The hybrid animals have gone quiet: lark-moths, fox-bats, all of them holding their breath the way you are holding yours. Something is keeping pace with you in the brush, and it is not an animal.
gmNotes: This is dread into snap: quiet, tell, roll, ambush.
Mercy carryover is a mechanical reward, but the exact canon weight remains a Kyle confirmation flag.
gmScript: Say: "The forest has gone quiet in a way your bodies understand before your minds do. Make an Instinct roll against Difficulty 14. Beat it and you see them before they move. Miss it and they get the jump." If the strixwolf was calmed or helped, add: "A distant hoot gives you one heartbeat of warning. Take an advantage die." If the strixwolf was killed or left blood-debt behind, add: "The forest gives no warning this time."
gmReadAloud: The road feels watched.
A branch snaps where no wind moved it.
Something is keeping pace with you in the brush, and it is not an animal.
gmChecklist: Read strixwolf_outcome, strixwolf_trust, and strixwolf_blood_debt.
Run Instinct 14.
Set ambushAwareness to see-them-coming or ambushed.
Move directly to MAP-S02-03 / S02-03 after the result.
gmPrivate: The watchers are nervous and organized, not monsters.
A high roll can reveal salvaged corporate gear without naming the deeper truth.
playerTakeaway: Your attention right now decides whether the encounter starts on your terms or theirs.
storyTakeaway: The hunters are close enough to act; the road has become a trap with a heartbeat of warning.
mechanicTakeaway: This is an Instinct 14 reaction/spot check; strixwolf mercy can grant an advantage die or lower pressure.

title: Cargo Reclaimer Ambush Battlefield
alt: Bramble Union Ambush Battlefield map board.
caption: A blocked forest road with hidden bramble lanes, carriage objective, and reclaimers trying to reach the Keystone cargo.
gmGoal: Run the ambush board as objective pressure around the carriage and a moral exit, not a static melee.
publicObjective: The road tightens into an ambush site: mud under the carriage wheels, thorn cover on both sides, and figures moving between the brush and the cargo line. The path forward is blocked by people, not beasts.
readAloud: The road tightens into an ambush site: mud under the carriage wheels, thorn cover on both sides, and figures moving between the brush and the cargo line. The path forward is blocked by people, not beasts.
gmNotes: The Union self-name is GM/earned dialogue. Player-facing board title stays Road Ambush.
Use Back Off to create space or protect the leader, not as a slaughter button.
gmScript: Say: "Use this board as pressure around the carriage. The attackers are trying to reach the package, not win a duel. Every round, a PC can fight, protect, reposition, spare someone, or roll Presence 15 to de-escalate."
gmReadAloud: The road tightens into an ambush site.
Mud pulls at the carriage wheels, thorn cover breaks sightlines, and figures move between brush and cargo line.
The path forward is blocked by people, not beasts.
gmChecklist: Apply ambushAwareness for first actor and starting distance.
Name the objective: the package in the carriage.
Offer Presence 15 de-escalation every round.
Lower social Difficulty for strixwolf mercy or sparing a downed attacker.
Resolve to S02-04 with bramble_outcome recorded.
gmPrivate: The ambushers fight like frightened amateurs because they are workers pushed into violence.
Letting them take the package is valid but costly. Do not block it; record it as a branch problem.
playerTakeaway: The road tightens into an ambush site: mud under the carriage wheels, thorn cover on both sides, and figures moving between the brush and the cargo line. The path forward is blocked by people, not beasts.
storyTakeaway: The board makes the moral shape of the ambush visible: desperate people, a vulnerable carriage, and an objective everyone can point to.
mechanicTakeaway: Combat, de-escalation, non-lethal control, Help an Ally, and objective defense are all live mechanics on this map.

sensorySummary: A blocked road, carriage cover, bramble lanes, muddy ruts, and figures moving between thorn-shadow and cargo line.
Raised voices from cover, reins snapping, thorns scratching armor and cloth, and the carriage wood groaning whenever pressure shifts.
Wet bramble, mud, horse sweat, torn leather, crushed leaves, and the sharp green smell of cut vines.
The road sucks at boots; brambles catch sleeves; carriage rails are smooth where hands can brace or climb.
The ambushers are people with homes and fear behind them. Their movement should feel trained by survival, not villain staging.
interactables: The staged cart: cover and proof the ambush was planned.
The thorn walls: cover, hazard, and flanking lanes.
The carriage: the objective everyone cares about.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The module's first real combat and the Bramble Union reveal. The overturned cart was a staged distraction; Bramble Union reclaimers ambush the party to steal the carriage holding the delivery. Teaches: battle-map setup, the Ambush reaction, reference stat blocks, and the spotted-vs-ambushed branch (an Instinct 14 roll decides who acts first).
locationSlideModel.readAloud: In a whirlwind of cracking branches and unsheathed steel, four figures rise from the brush alongside the road. The overturned cart was an ambush all along. They stand before you, weapons drawn, blocking the way — and they move first.

sensoryStack.detail: Four Bramblefolk; armor made of polished river stones; daggers; thorny bramble worked into their gear; the staged cart behind them.
Branches snapping, steel leaving sheaths, a sharp whistle between the ambushers .
green sap, crushed thorn, sweat — people who live rough in the deep preserve.
Adrenaline; the road suddenly narrow; the carriage a prize behind the party.
The forest goes quiet (animals scatter from the violence).

optionalRolls.Notes: Canon (p.30). Success → "See Them Coming," PCs act first; with Fear, +1 Fear and mark Stress. Failure → "Ambushed!", Bramblefolk act first; with Fear, +1 Fear + Stress.

optionalRolls.Action: Describe your attack / evasion in detail
optionalRolls.Notes: Canon GM prompt (p.30): invite players to narrate, build the scene collaboratively.

optionalRolls.Action: Try to talk them down mid-fight
optionalRolls.Notes: The Bramblefolk are desperate, not evil (p.28). A PC who realizes this could de-escalate — success thins the fight or opens a parley. Reinforces the module's "they are hungry, not villains" theme.
The thief's whole goal is the carriage; a PC can body-block the theft.

fearEvents: The thief's Back Off action (spend Fear): attack all targets in Melee, push successes into Far range, 2d6+3 magic. Use it to break a PC away from defending the carriage.
Spend Fear: a fifth, unseen reclaimer cuts a carriage horse loose to slow pursuit — raises stakes without adding a combatant.
Theme reminder: these are neighbors treated as thieves because official routes starve them out (p.28). Let mercy be mechanically possible.
locationSlideModel.combatBlock:
Setup (p.30): Lay the cut-out forest terrain across the table collaboratively; place the overturned vendor cart; players position their minis near the carriage; put Bramble Ambusher standees + the Bramble Thief in Close range.
Bramble Ambusher — Tier 1 Standard (Reference stat block, ×3)
Dagger: Melee, 1d8+5 phy · ATK +1 · Difficulty 13 · HP 3 · Stress 2 · Thresholds 6/12
Ambush (Reaction): entering unspotted, immediately move to Melee + attack; on success, dagger for 2d4+8 phy.
Ambusher attack guide: roll d20 +1 vs Evasion; hit → 1d8+5; compare thresholds, apply armor, mark HP.
Bramble Thief — Tier 1 Leader
Serrated Blade: Melee, 2d4+3 phy · ATK +3 · Difficulty 14 · HP 4 · Stress 0 · Thresholds 7/14
Back Off (Action): spend a Fear, attack all in Melee; successes blasted to Far range, 2d6+3 magic.
Thief attack guide: d20 +3 vs Evasion; hit → 2d4+3; on a Back-Off success deal damage and shove the PC.
Defense guide: compare damage to thresholds, mark HP; last HP marked = defeated.
The Union's goal: ambushers hold attention while the thief steals the carriage.
End: when all adversaries fall, clear the map; have PCs narrate a travel montage to Hush.
transitions: In: From 02, triggered by clearing/leaving the cart or by the Instinct 14 result.
Out: Encounter ends → travel montage → 04_Hush_Enclave.

gmDetails.title: Road choke
gmDetails.body: The carriage sits in the center. Mud and wreckage create difficult footing. Thorn walls limit sightlines and make flanking plausible.

gmDetails.title: Moral exit
gmDetails.body: Presence 15 can thin or end the fight. Strixwolf mercy, sparing a downed attacker, or naming the fact that the attackers want cargo instead of lives can lower the Difficulty.

gmDetails.title: Objective pressure
gmDetails.body: Every round should ask what happens to the carriage and package: protected, threatened, moved, cut off, or surrendered.

gmChecklist: Apply ambushAwareness for first actor and starting distance.

gmPrivate: The ambushers fight like frightened amateurs because they are workers pushed into violence.
Letting them take the package is valid but costly. Do not block it; record it as a branch problem.
combatFraming: Reluctant aggressors: they want the cargo, not a massacre.
See-Them-Coming means PCs act first or can call out before blades move. Ambushed means the attackers begin closer and act first.
Parley is a live action every round: Presence 15. Mercy lowers the Difficulty.
They do not fight to the death. At half strength, after a non-lethal leader down, or after a credible parley, survivors break, surrender, or negotiate.

perCharacterLayer.passive: Reads the fight as a line to hold, not a hunt to win.

title: The Ambush
alt: The Ambush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
caption: The road ambush should feel dangerous and understandable at the same time.
gmGoal: Run the ambush as a dangerous moral choice: fight, defend, flee, surrender, or talk it down.
publicObjective: Survive the ambush and protect the carriage and the package.
readAloud: Four figures rise from the brush in a clatter of breaking branches: ragged, wiry, armored in lashed river-stone and thorn. Their blades are mismatched, half of them salvaged. A fifth hangs back, sharper-eyed, clearly the one giving orders. They do not whoop or charge. They block the road, weapons up, like people who hate that it has come to this. "The cargo," the leader says. "Hand it over and you walk."
gmNotes: The leader does not want a massacre.
Use Back Off to create space and panic, not to punish parley.
A downed ambusher can be spared without a roll; that lowers social difficulty.
gmScript: Say: "They want the cargo, not your lives. You can fight, defend the carriage, run, surrender the package, or talk while weapons are up. If you talk, make the case in character and roll Presence against Difficulty 15." If they ask who they are and the conversation earns it, have the leader say: "We're the Bramble Union. We didn't used to be thieves."
gmReadAloud: Four figures rise from the brush in a clatter of breaking branches: ragged, wiry, armored in lashed river-stone and thorn.
A fifth hangs back, sharper-eyed, clearly the one giving orders.
"The cargo," the leader says. "Hand it over and you walk."
gmChecklist: Apply ambushAwareness from S02-02.
Explicitly offer parley as a live action.
Use Presence 15 for de-escalation; lower it for mercy, spared foes, or strong leverage.
Record bramble_outcome using existing enum: killed, captured, spared, negotiated, escaped.
Do not say Keystone Asset in player-facing text.
gmPrivate: The self-name is earned through dialogue. The public/corporate label remains Cargo Reclaimers until that moment.
Their salvaged gear points to former company people, but do not over-explain the hidden plot in combat.
If players choose slaughter, they win the fight and lose the easiest route to the truth.
playerTakeaway: You can win this with steel, restraint, surrender, or words, and the choice defines who the party is.
storyTakeaway: The attackers are desperate people who want the cargo more than blood; their humanity is visible before their story is clear.
mechanicTakeaway: This combat tracks an outcome, not a body count: Presence de-escalation, non-lethal choices, and bramble_outcome all matter.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You can win this with steel, restraint, surrender, or words, and the choice defines who the party is.
player.say: "Blade, bargain, shield, or surrender - all of those can end this. Pick the one your character can live with."
player.ask: "You can attack, protect the carriage, try Presence 15 to talk them down, spare a downed attacker, run, or hand over the package and deal with the fallout."
player.deeper: Make all exits real. The players should feel that victory is defined by consequences, not by eliminating every enemy.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The attackers are desperate people who want the cargo more than blood; their humanity is visible before their story is clear.
story.say: "They look scared and committed, not gleeful. That does not make them safe. It makes them people."
story.ask: "If the leader speaks honestly, she can give the self-name: Bramble Union. If nobody earns that moment, keep them as Cargo Reclaimers or ambushers in player-facing language."
story.deeper: This is the earned disclosure point. Use dialogue to reveal the name, never narration before the table creates the opening.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: This combat tracks an outcome, not a body count: Presence de-escalation, non-lethal choices, and bramble_outcome all matter.
mechanic.say: "Presence 15 can end this fight. Mercy shown earlier or now can lower the difficulty. Killing is not the only resolution the rules care about."
mechanic.ask: "Set bramble_outcome: killed, captured, spared, negotiated, or escaped. That flag changes S02-04 and whether the location maps open."
mechanic.deeper: Use HP and Stress for danger, but use bramble_outcome for meaning. The map, adversaries, Fear features, and social off-ramp all serve that outcome.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Ambush
playerSafeProjection.alt: The Ambush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The road ambush should feel dangerous and understandable at the same time.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Survive the ambush and protect the carriage and the package.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: Four figures rise from the brush in a clatter of breaking branches: ragged, wiry, armored in lashed river-stone and thorn. Their blades are mismatched, half of them salvaged. A fifth hangs back, sharper-eyed, clearly the one giving orders. They do not whoop or charge. They block the road, weapons up, like people who hate that it has come to this. "The cargo," the leader says. "Hand it over and you walk."

perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Garrick, they clock you as ex-company before you say much. Want to speak from that truth?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Sees how to move with shifting cover instead of fighting it.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Barnacle, this maze has rules like an alley that is alive. Want to follow the gap before it closes?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Hears the briar opening and closing before the eye catches it.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Varian, the thorns move like breath. Want to guide the group by sound and scent?

perCharacterLayer.passive: Her restraint on the road matters here; people watch whether her size means threat or shelter.
perCharacterLayer.playerCue: Khari, they are deciding whether your strength is danger or protection. What do you show them?

title: After the Ambush
alt: After the Ambush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
caption: After the fight, the module asks what victory cost and what the party learned.
gmGoal: Turn the outcome of the ambush into consequence, truth, and the next route toward the village.
publicObjective: Decide what to do with what just happened and get the package moving again.
readAloud: The brush goes still. Whatever you did, it is done. The horses breathe hard. The road smells like wet thorn, churned mud, and adrenaline fading too slowly. Among what was dropped, you see gear that does not look like bandit scrap: stamped buckles, route tags, and filed-off inventory marks from the same kind of system that hired you.
gmNotes: Mercy route: leader or survivors talk.
Combat route: gear and effects talk.
Either route should leave the party asking who benefits from a dangerous forest.
gmScript: Say: "The fight is over. The outcome matters now." If mercy or negotiation opened trust, say: "Up close, these people look less like bandits and more like former workers who have been sleeping rough and losing for a long time." If the party killed or routed them, say: "The gear tells the story the survivors cannot: company issue, filed off and reused." If players ask for the truth, use Presence or Knowledge 14, or mercy already earned, to reveal: "They were company or preserve workers who say the danger reports were manufactured to sell protection and discard the people who noticed."
gmReadAloud: The brush goes still. Whatever you did, it is done.
Among what was dropped, you see gear that does not look like bandit scrap: stamped buckles, route tags, and filed-off inventory marks.
The road smells like wet thorn, churned mud, and adrenaline fading too slowly.
gmChecklist: Read bramble_outcome before choosing variant tone.
Set bramble_truth_learned only if mercy/parley, survivor dialogue, or Presence/Knowledge 14 earns it.
Unlock location maps only for spared, negotiated, captured-with-care, or escaped-with-contact routes.
Give a thread, not the whole campaign explanation.
gmPrivate: The workers' claim is the first load-bearing truth thread, but the driver-killer canon flag remains unresolved.
Do not mention Keystone Asset in player-facing aftermath.
If players pursue the communities, use the two location maps as optional discovery, not mandatory plot.
playerTakeaway: You do not have the whole picture, but you have seen enough to question who benefits from a dangerous forest.
storyTakeaway: The attackers were tied to the same company world that hired the party; the forest's danger story no longer matches the evidence.
mechanicTakeaway: The mechanic here is consequence: bramble_outcome and bramble_truth_learned decide what doors open next.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You do not have the whole picture, but you have seen enough to question who benefits from a dangerous forest.

story.title: Story takeaway

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway

title: Act Three: Seeking a Custodian
caption: Hush turns the package from cargo into a community question.
gmGoal: Shift from road peril to a warm village sanctuary, then let the contrast carry unease. Establish the job plainly: reach Hush, find the person who keeps it safe, and deliver the package.
publicObjective: Reach the village, find the person who can receive the package, and deliver it.
readAloud: The road softens. The trees do not change, but the air does: warmer, kinder, like a held breath finally letting go. Ahead, lantern-light and music gather around ordinary people who feel safe. Somewhere in this village is the person you were sent to find. All you have to do now is hand off the package and collect your pay. Simple.
gmNotes: High mercy from earlier acts starts Hush warmer. Slaughter or extraction starts Hush polite but cooler.
If package_status is lost, this act can still play as arrival and social discovery, but the handoff branch is blocked until Kyle confirms the recovery path.
playerTakeaway: You have reached the safe place; the job is nearly done, but the village is worth noticing before you rush through it.
storyTakeaway: Hush is the haven the delivery exists to serve, and its safety is deliberate rather than accidental.
mechanicTakeaway: Act 3 runs on social and exploration mechanics: Presence for trust, Instinct for unease, Knowledge for ward and infrastructure clues.

title: Arrival at Hush
alt: Arrival at Hush scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
caption: Hush must land as a warm place with jokes inside it, not as the joke.
gmGoal: Run the ward-boundary crossing, the first welcome, and the first read of how prior choices affect Hush trust.
publicObjective: Enter the village, get your bearings, and find the person who keeps this place safe.
readAloud: A tall stone pillar rises beside the road, carved top to bottom with old protective marks and newer brass stamps. As the carriage passes it, you feel a small sensation like a bubble popping. The forest hush gives way to friendly chatter, tavern music, and smiling faces turning to wave you in. The trees are still colossal, but here the air feels safe. What do you do?
gmNotes: Hush people are sincere. Company marks are the unease.
Player-safe language: old protective marks, newer official stamps, the ward, the package.
gmScript: Say: "That bubble-pop is the ward. You just crossed into protected ground. If you arrived with mercy behind you, the welcome feels warmer. If the road behind you was bloodier, the welcome is polite but watchful."
gmReadAloud: A tall stone pillar rises beside the road, carved with old protective marks and newer brass stamps.
As the carriage passes it, you feel a small sensation like a bubble popping.
The forest hush gives way to friendly chatter, tavern music, and smiling faces turning to wave you in.
gmChecklist: Read strixwolf_outcome / strixwolf_disposition, bramble_outcome, bramble_truth_learned, and package_status.
Set hush_trust baseline: high for mercy/parley, neutral for unknown, low for slaughter/extraction.
Set ward_awareness to seed after the bubble-pop.
If package_status is lost, name the blocked handoff privately and do not invent the recovery branch.
gmPrivate: The brass stamps are corporate registration; keep that as a sharp-PC/GMer seed, not a player-facing explanation.
If package_status=lost, the party can still seek the person who keeps Hush safe, but the normal handoff cannot resolve until Kyle confirms the recovery branch.
playerTakeaway: You are inside protected ground, and the village is watching how you arrive.
storyTakeaway: The ward is real, felt, and connected to the job before anyone explains how.
mechanicTakeaway: First impressions are a mechanic here: carry-in choices set hush_trust, while Presence or Instinct 12 can read the welcome.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
official_results.success_with_hope: Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: Hush becomes a service endpoint instead of a home. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You are inside protected ground, and the village is watching how you arrive.

story.statement: The ward is real, felt, and connected to the job before anyone explains how.

mechanic.ask: "Success tells you whether Hush is warm, watchful, or already nervous about you. Mercy on the road makes that warmth easier to earn."
mechanic.deeper: Use state visibly: set hush_trust from carry-in, then let the players improve or damage it through how they enter.

caption: Visual reference for Hush.
gmGoal: Use Hush as the warm hub for Act 3: a lived-in village, ward boundary, social routes, and all optional detours looping back toward the keeper.
publicObjective: Hush gathers under the colossal trees: warm windows, lantern branches, low roofs, and paths leading toward a tree-tavern, market stalls, festival noise, and the farms beyond.
readAloud: Hush gathers under the colossal trees: warm windows, lantern branches, low roofs, and paths leading toward a tree-tavern, market stalls, festival noise, and the farms beyond.
gmNotes: No dead ends: co-op, market, festival, farms, and official sign all loop back here or forward to the keeper route.
gmScript: Say: "Use this as the hub. From here the party can head to the Co-op, ask locals, visit the market or festival, inspect the farms, or follow directions south when custodian_route is set."
gmReadAloud: Hush gathers under the colossal trees.
Warm windows and lantern branches make it feel lived in.
Every path here should either deepen trust or point back toward the keeper.
gmChecklist: Keep detours looped back to the hub.
Use player-safe Hush in player text.
Treat the official/corporate lens as GM-only or sharp-PC discovery.
gmPrivate: The cozy hub is a registered managed place. Keep that hidden-truth lens off the player display until discovered.

sensorySummary: Low roofs, shoe lines, kitchen windows, repair benches, clover charms, and ward posts make the village feel guarded but lived in.
Mugs clink indoors, children whisper behind trusted adults, a distant work song falters when the ward hum misses a beat.
Bread, wet clover, hearth smoke, clean laundry, and a mineral edge from ward fixtures working too hard.
Packed earth is softened by moss; doorframes are polished by hands; the air warms near kitchens and cools near ward posts.
People notice everything without making a scene. Dogs, children, elders, and workers keep adjusting around the party's choices.
visibleDetails: A village built for working hands, with shoes lined near thresholds and adults quietly tracking the sealed crate.
Children watch from behind people they trust; nobody runs, but nobody relaxes until the party proves how they arrived.
subtleDetails: The ward chimes lag half a beat behind each other.
Corporate plaques use the trademarked name, while locals speak around it like an old irritation.

Too much pressure about the ward makes locals go quiet.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The roleplay and breather hub. A warded village of warmth and music where the party must find the Whitefire Custodian by talking to locals. This is the social heart of the one-shot — three named NPCs, a vertical tavern, an optional festival, and the strongest "ask the players to build it with you" beat in the module.
locationSlideModel.readAloud: The path leads deeper until a tall stone pillar rises beside the road — carved top to bottom in old dwarven symbols, studded with small brass compliance stamps. It marks one corner of Hush Community Enclave. As your carriage passes the marker, you feel a small sensation, like a bubble popping, and the forest's hush gives way to the sound of people: friendly chatter, lively music drifting from a tavern at the center of town. The trees here are the same colossal preserve-trees, but the air feels safe, comforting. Smiling faces turn as you roll in, waving, calling warm greetings. Somewhere in this town is the Custodian you were sent to find. What do you do?

sensoryStack.detail: Carved dwarven ward-pillar with brass compliance stamps; lantern-strung branches; a tavern (the Clover Co-op) built up the trunk of an ancient tree; shoes hung on a line across the bar's ground floor.
Music, laughter, good-natured conversation, the creak of the tavern's wooden levels.
Ask the players (canon, p.32): "What smell permeates the air throughout this place?" Pre-loaded fallback : woodsmoke, fresh bread, spilled ale, moss.
The "bubble pop" of crossing the ward; warmth; safety after the road.
Children lighting lanterns in the branches; a clank playing an unknown card-and-acorn game; a bearded dwarf hauling an ale barrel on one shoulder.

optionalRolls.Notes: Canon: shoes returned shined and filled with small trinkets by the time they leave. Pure charm — reward curiosity.

gmDetails.title: Named NPCs (GM-only, canon p.32)
gmDetails.body:
Fidget — Wildborne Human, they/them. A young child who will not stop wiggling; scurries up trees lighting lanterns; knows the fastest routes through town; curious what life is like outside Hush.
Lausa Standworth — Wildborne Dwarf, she/her. Older woman, thick beard, hauls an ale barrel on her shoulder the entire conversation. Wants to know the name of every party member's weapon and the date it was forged.
Halython Fives — Loreborne Clank (humanoid robot), he/him. Soft-spoken, scratches on one metal shoulder where a friendly fox-bat perches. Plays an unknown card-and-acorn game. Asks about the Bramble Union.
Use one to make first contact, a second as the friend who knows where the Custodian lives.

gmDetails.body: If the party arrives early, Hush is mid-festival: the Sunless Farms crops have grown their first moss layer (ripening for the season). Arm-wrestling competition, a stone-painting class, a small marketplace of homemade trinkets. A full breather scene if the table wants downtime.

sensorySummary: A polished official sign and neat route stones frame a village that keeps interrupting the label with charms, scuffed paths, and hand repairs.
The entry ward hums unevenly; someone inside laughs, then lowers their voice; a sign chain taps in the damp wind.
Damp paint, moss, warm bread from deeper in town, and the brass smell of a ward fixture under strain.
The sign is smooth and cold; the handmade charms are waxed, rough, and thumb-worn from being touched.
Locals move through the entrance by habit, using the paths they trust instead of the lines the sign wants them to use.
visibleDetails: A polished sign uses the trademarked name; someone has hung a hand-painted clover charm over one corner.
The route stones are neat near the entrance and messier where residents actually walk.
subtleDetails: Locals do not correct the name every time; they choose when the correction matters.
The cleanest sign is also the least touched object in view.
hazards: Using the official label casually chills local warmth.
Pushing records too hard makes watchers close the room.

sensorySummary: Green lanterns, damp banners, mossfruit baskets, children's game stones, and adults keeping lanes clear without calling it guarding.
Work songs, clapping, small feet on mud, griddle hiss, and the sudden dip in music whenever the ward hum catches wrong.
Sweet mossfruit, hot griddle cakes, trampled clover, rain on lantern paper, and smoke from cookfires kept low.
Mud is springy under moss; ribbons brush faces; lantern paper goes soft at the edges in the wet air.
This is joy with watchfulness inside it. Let children, cooks, elders, and workers make the stakes visible before the crisis.
visibleDetails: Green lanterns, clover cakes, damp banners, and work songs turn the lane into a celebration.
Adults keep the route clear without making it look like guarding.
subtleDetails: A few smiles falter when the ward hum dips.
Older locals track the Keystone crate even while passing food.
hazards: Bad road news can turn joy into fear.
Mocking the festival cools trust.
Pushing farm questions too hard draws watched silence.

Irrigation trickles under boards, insects drone in the damp rows, and farmers pause whenever a weak ward post changes pitch.
Mushroom loam, damp leaves, cold channel water, cut stems, and the mineral bite of mosslit irrigation.
Soil is soft, dark, and springy; leaves feel waxy from low light; tool handles are polished by wet hands.
Field workers, insects, and crop behavior are the warning system. The farms should feel intelligent, not quaint.
visibleDetails: Blue-green rows grow in carefully shaded beds.
Farm tools hang under low roofs where rain and sap cannot ruin them.
subtleDetails: The healthiest crops cluster near older local water paths.
Corporate survey stakes stand where no farmer would plant.
hazards: Rushing damages irrigation.
Too many corporate questions make crews stop talking.
The route south is unclear without local guidance.

checks.prompt: Instinct 13: the abundance is carefully managed, not wild.
Knowledge 13: farm-magic and ward-work share a signature.
Finesse 12 if the party moves quickly through fragile channels.

fearSpends: A row dims as the Keystone passes.
A survey stake hums louder than the ward post.
mapData.storyTakeaway: The farms show that Hush's abundance is cultivated, protected, and vulnerable.
mapData.mechanicTakeaway: Instinct or Knowledge 13 can find the farm/ward seed; Finesse keeps the party from trampling fragile work.

sensoryStack.detail: Pale moss rows under shade, dark soil, blue waterlines, and practical tools.
Dripping channels, quiet crew calls, and the low scrape of farm work.
Damp earth, green moss, mineral water, and crushed stems.
Cool, cultivated, protected, and just a little too orderly.
Workers know exactly where to step and watch whether strangers do.

gmScript: Say: "This is the room where Hush decides whether the party belongs for tonight. Offer shoes, food, a game, and one regular by description before name."
gmReadAloud: Tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, and chipped mugs.
A room full of people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
gmChecklist: Offer the shoe line.
Use at least one regular.
Ask one tavern-building prompt.
Let the room react to bramble_outcome if it comes up.

playerTakeaway: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
storyTakeaway: The Co-op turns Hush from a destination into people with customs and boundaries.
mechanicTakeaway: Presence, Prepare/Hope, and table spotlight are enough to make this scene mechanically alive.

mapData.title: Clover Co-op Location Map
mapData.caption: Visual reference for Clover Co-op.
mapData.playerText: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
mapData.readAloud: Inside the village, the Co-op is a warm public room of tea steam, shoe lines, gift shelves, chipped mugs, and people deciding whether these travelers are guests, trouble, or both.
mapData.gmGoal: Run the Co-op as a social hub: shoe custom, regulars, games, tavern prompts, and trust-building.
sensorySummary: Mismatched chairs face inward, shoe lines mark the threshold, and gift shelves hold jars, cloth, ribbons, and careful generosity.
Tea pours, mugs knock softly, someone clears their throat before hard news, and a ward chime outside lands a little flat.
Clover honey, tea steam, wet boot leather, old wood warmed by bodies, and food stretched with pride instead of abundance.
Counters are nicked smooth; mugs are chipped in familiar places; wool sleeves stay damp near the door.
The room tracks manners. People make space, stop talking, resume talking, and decide whether the party is safe to feed.
visibleDetails: Mismatched chairs face the room instead of the door.
Shoes, jars, folded cloth, and festival ribbons sit in tidy little systems that locals understand immediately.
subtleDetails: People notice who says thank you and who reaches before being offered.
The gift shelves are sparse but maintained with pride.
hazards: Taking hospitality as entitlement lowers trust.
Road news can turn warmth into grief.
Mocking customs closes doors.

title: Local Clues
alt: Local Clues scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
caption: Local clues make the infrastructure failure personal and specific.
gmGoal: Run the objective spine: talk to locals, build trust, find the route to the person who keeps Hush safe, and seed the watched/corporate unease.
publicObjective: Find someone who can point you toward the person who keeps the ward working.
readAloud: The town is happy to talk. Everyone seems to know the person you are looking for, though they are protective of her. A friendly local can point the way, if the town decides you are safe enough to send toward someone it loves.
gmNotes: S03-02 must set custodian_route; this is the Act 3 to Act 4 hinge.
Bramble truth learned makes sharper questions land; if false, let contradictions still be visible.
gmScript: Say: "They know who you mean, but they do not hand beloved people to strangers just because the strangers have a contract. Talk to them. Let them decide whether you are guests, customers, or trouble."
gmReadAloud: The town is happy to talk.
Everyone seems to know the person you are looking for, though they are protective of her.
A friendly local can point the way, if the town decides you are safe enough.
gmChecklist: Use description before NPC names: wiggling lantern-child, bearded ale-hauler, quiet clank with a fox-bat.
Set custodian_route by trust: safe, dangerous, or unknown.
Set hush_clues when the party earns a route, ward seed, corporate seam, farm seed, or market rumor.
If players push on the ward/company, offer one brave thread and one watched-room cost.
gmPrivate: Hush is watched. A brave local can hint at official paperwork, managed farms, or nervous ward maintenance, then shut down when a minder is near.
Do not name the full ward economy or the Keystone. The strongest player-safe phrase is: the ward keeps Hush safe, and people are worried about it.
playerTakeaway: The way to the keeper runs through the town's trust, not through contract authority.
storyTakeaway: Hush will help the party reach the person it protects, but only after the party treats Hush like people.
mechanicTakeaway: This is social investigation: Presence earns directions, Instinct reads what gets dodged, and Knowledge reads ward or infrastructure clues.

entities.name: Fidget
entities.summary: A restless child who knows fast routes through the village and asks blunt questions.
entities.role: Warm local guide and pace reset.
entities.playerDisplayCaption: a restless child guide who knows the fastest ways through the village
entities.personality: Restless, sharp, and starved to be useful before the grown-ups decide the useful part is over. Reads people fast and forgives slow. The bead strings are a walking map only Fidget can fully read: blue for water, brass for tolls, bone-white for the places adults say children should not go.
entities.wants: Be useful before grown-ups decide the useful part is over.
entities.sampleLine: You walk like people who got told where to go by a form.

block2.animal_companion: No animal; the trinket bandolier rattles like a little parade.

block3.how_they_expect_pcs_to_behave: Fidget expects the PCs to need help and pretend they do not.

what_moves_them.result: Fidget gives the cleanest local route and one blunt warning.

block2.personality: Patient to the point of disguise, hiding hard questions inside a children's game of cards and acorns. Oils the same shoulder twice when nervous. Wants, more than anything, to be a person made of parts rather than a tool that happened to learn tricks.
voice: The acorn goes there if you are hoping, here if you are lying.
I asked about the Bramble because everyone else stopped asking out loud.
No, the fox-bat is not cheating. I am.
block2.secrets: Halython knows more sympathy for the displaced than a safe public table permits.
block2.fears: Being treated as a tool that happened to learn card tricks.

likes_dislikes.likes: Fair games, repaired hinges, quiet players, and fox-bat gossip.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep.
Firstmoss and the Sunless Farms show the forest feeding Hush rather than hunting it.
An elder says, "The wood was never this bad. The trouble came with the waymarkers."
A ledger shows protection costs and hazard sightings climbing together.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: The way to the keeper runs through the town's trust, not through contract authority.
player.say: "Be someone they would send to a beloved protector. That is the route."
player.ask: "A gentle question, a favor, honest road news, or joining a local custom can earn directions. A demand gets you only vague southward pointing."

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: Hush will help the party reach the person it protects, but only after the party treats Hush like people.
story.say: "They are not hiding her to be difficult. They are protecting somebody who protects them."
story.ask: "Low trust means: south, past the farms. Neutral trust means a clear path. High trust means a guide and the safe irrigation route."
story.deeper: This is the act hinge. The story payoff is not just finding a location; it is whether the town vouches for the party before Act 4.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: This is social investigation: Presence earns directions, Instinct reads what gets dodged, and Knowledge reads ward or infrastructure clues.
mechanic.say: "Presence earns the route. Instinct catches the dodge. Knowledge reads the ward marks and logistics. Pick the tool that matches what you actually do."
mechanic.ask: "For directions, use Presence 12 if uncertain. For the watched/corporate seam, use Instinct or Knowledge 13. Success sets custodian_route or ward_awareness."
mechanic.deeper: Record the mechanical consequence immediately: custodian_route safe/dangerous/unknown, ward_awareness none/seed/aware, and hush_clues for what they learned.

Let ordinary people, animals, chores, and hospitality react to the party so the place feels inhabited.

caption: The Clover Co-op gives the party hospitality, texture, and reasons to care.
gmGoal: Use the vertical tavern as Hush's social heart: shoe custom, named locals, player-authored details, and a chance to belong.
publicObjective: Rest, connect, and become someone the town trusts.
readAloud: The Clover Co-op climbs the trunk of an ancient tree, level stacked on level, crowded with music and good-natured noise. A friendly local stops you at the door: newcomers hang their shoes on the line strung across the ground floor. By the time you leave, locals promise, the shoes come back shined and filled with little trinkets. Warmth, food, and a dozen conversations wait. What do you do?
gmNotes: This scene is relationship, not objective extraction. Slow down and let players be people.
Do not turn hospitality into shopping inventory; use gifts as story boons.
gmScript: Say: "This is Hush's living room. Hang your shoes if you want to honor the custom. Pick a face, pick a table, or tell me one thing this tavern has that no tavern outside Hush would have."
gmReadAloud: The Clover Co-op climbs the trunk of an ancient tree.
Newcomers hang their shoes on the line strung across the ground floor.
Warmth, food, and a dozen conversations wait.
gmChecklist: Offer the shoe custom and reward it later with polished, trinket-filled shoes.
Describe Fidget, Lausa, and Halython before naming them.
Ask one player-authored tavern prompt.
Offer Prepare/Hope as a quiet breather.
Let Halython ask about the road outcome when the moment is warm.
gmPrivate: Halython's Bramble question lets bramble_outcome affect trust without lore-dumping.
Even the tavern has small protective wards; Marlowe can notice this.
playerTakeaway: This is the warm center of the act: a place to be people before being couriers again.
storyTakeaway: Belonging in Hush is offered through customs, food, games, and careful attention.
mechanicTakeaway: Downtime is mechanical here: Prepare/Hope, Presence, and respectful roleplay can raise hush_trust and unlock a guide.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: This is the warm center of the act: a place to be people before being couriers again.
player.say: "Put the job down for a minute. Be a person. Hush is watching kindly."

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: Belonging in Hush is offered through customs, food, games, and careful attention.
story.say: "They are not testing you with a form. They are seeing whether you can be gentle with their home."
story.ask: "Halython may ask what happened with the road attackers. A mercy answer warms the room. A bloody answer makes people quieter."
story.deeper: Let the Bramble carry-in affect faces and tone, not a lecture. The town can be kind and still judge the party's choices.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Downtime is mechanical here: Prepare/Hope, Presence, and respectful roleplay can raise hush_trust and unlock a guide.
mechanic.say: "A breather can be a move. If you Prepare, name what care looks like and bank the Hope according to the table's rules."
mechanic.ask: "Presence 10 can honor the custom if uncertain. A warm roleplay beat can raise hush_trust without dice when it is obvious."
mechanic.deeper: The concrete payoff is goodwill: raised hush_trust, a guide candidate, festival access, or a small trinket/favor later.
