title: Firstmoss Launch Festival
alt: Firstmoss Launch Festival scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
caption: Firstmoss makes the stakes joyous before the module asks the party to defend them.
gmGoal: Offer the optional reward arc: a joyful festival, low-stakes contests, a concrete boon, and one quiet seed about the farms.
publicObjective: Join the celebration if you want, earn goodwill, and gather what helps for the road ahead.
readAloud: You have arrived during the Firstmoss Launch Festival. The town celebrates the season's first moss rising on the Sunless Farms crops, the promise of fresh fruit and full tables ahead. There is a good-natured arm-wrestling competition, a stone-painting class, and a small market of homemade trinkets. The whole village feels lighter for a moment. What do you do?
gmNotes: The festival is the act's exhale before the Act 4 turn.
Boon examples: charm, favor token, useful market find, or goodwill that opens a door later.
gmScript: Say: "This festival is optional, but it is real. If you join in, Hush remembers. Arm-wrestle, paint a stone, browse the market, dance badly, ask about the farms, or skip it and keep moving."
gmReadAloud: You have arrived during the Firstmoss Launch Festival.
There is arm-wrestling, stone-painting, and a small market of homemade trinkets.
The whole village feels lighter for a moment.
gmChecklist: Frame festival participation as optional.
Grant a concrete festival_boon for sincere participation or a contest win.
Let Khari/Varian/Barnacle/Marlowe hooks surface if those PCs are in play.
Only seed the farm/corporate thread if a player probes it.
Route back toward S03-02/MAP-LOC-hush-farms when ready.
gmPrivate: The Sunless Farms are managed infrastructure. Seed through crops, schedules, and volunteer precision; do not explain the ward economy.
Skipping the festival is an opportunity cost, not a punishment.
playerTakeaway: You get one genuinely good day; taking part can give the party goodwill and a small boon.
storyTakeaway: Hush's abundance is real and joyful, even if a curious player may notice how carefully it is managed.
mechanicTakeaway: Low-stakes mechanics still matter: Strength, Finesse, Presence, market choices, and Prepare/Hope can all produce a festival_boon.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You get one genuinely good day; taking part can give the party goodwill and a small boon.
player.say: "You have earned one good day. Spend a little of it here, and Hush may send something useful with you."
player.ask: "You can arm-wrestle, paint a stone, browse the market, ask about Firstmoss, or skip the festival and keep moving toward the keeper."
player.deeper: The player-facing choice is participation vs. momentum. Both are valid; only participation grants the boon.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: Hush's abundance is real and joyful, even if a curious player may notice how carefully it is managed.
story.say: "The joy is real. The food is real. A curious mind may still wonder who runs the farms that make it possible."
story.ask: "Player-safe answer: Firstmoss is the first ripening layer on the Sunless Farms crops. Sharp read: the farms run with unusual precision."
story.deeper: Seed managed abundance through detail only: schedules, crops, volunteers, branded stall, and people going quiet near official questions.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Low-stakes mechanics still matter: Strength, Finesse, Presence, market choices, and Prepare/Hope can all produce a festival_boon.
mechanic.say: "Arm-wrestling is Strength 12. Stone-painting or graceful mingling can be Finesse or Presence 12. A probing farm read is Instinct or Knowledge 13."

caption: The Custodian and the Hanging Office turn the delivery into a choice.
gmGoal: Turn the courier job into a calling. The party reaches the person who can receive the package, learns what it really is, and chooses whether to carry the danger forward.
publicObjective: Find the Custodian, deliver the package, and learn what comes next.
readAloud: The town thins behind you, fields giving way to forest again. The trees here wear faces, hundreds of them carved into the bark, eyes turned every direction. Somewhere past them lives the person you were sent to find. After everything the road asked of you, the last stretch is the strangest. Whatever is in that crate, you are about to learn why it mattered enough to send a crew to die for it.

title: Through the Farms
alt: Through the Farms scene art for The Hanging Office.
caption: The road through the farms shifts the story from delivery job to stewardship problem.
gmGoal: Cross from Hush farmland into the carved-face preserve edge and pay off the route the party earned.
publicObjective: Reach the Custodian's home.
readAloud: Past the last homes of the village, the crops change: fruits and vegetables wear a thin layer of glowing blue moss that pulses softly with warmth as you pass. Then the cultivated land ends, and the preserve returns. The great trees here have faces, hundreds of them, carved into every side. Ahead, something hangs in the canopy: a cabin, swaying gently, suspended over a counterweight stone the size of a cabin itself.
gmNotes: This is the Act 3 to Act 4 consequence handoff: route quality changes approach pressure.
The alternate hazard is minor and non-combat. Save lethal danger for Act 5.
gmScript: Say: "This is where the route you earned pays off. If Hush trusted you, the way is calm. If the route is dangerous or unknown, the preserve asks for one last bit of attention before the treehouse."
gmReadAloud: The crops wear a thin layer of glowing blue moss.
The cultivated land ends, and the preserve returns.
The great trees here have faces carved into every side.
gmChecklist: Read custodian_route before framing the path.
Safe route: guided calm, no roll.
Dangerous/unknown route: Instinct 13 or one minor Stress-level preserve hazard.
If strixwolf_blood_debt is true, make the carved faces feel hostile.
If package_status=lost, the approach can continue but the normal reveal is blocked.
gmPrivate: The carved faces are ward anchors. Seed them as texture now; let the Custodian explain later.
The moss shares the ward's magic. Do not explain the cost here.
playerTakeaway: You are leaving safe ground and approaching something old and watchful.
storyTakeaway: The Custodian's home sits at the strange heart of the preserve, where the ward's protection becomes visible.
mechanicTakeaway: custodian_route gates the approach: safe route skips the obstacle, dangerous or unknown route asks for Instinct 13 or costs 1 Stress.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.
"The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."
"Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear."
The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.
The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The reveal scene. The party meets the Whitefire Custodian — a seven-foot humanoid-firefly faerie — delivers the sealed crate, and learns the truth: it holds the Keystone Asset, the ward-stone for the entire capital city. Her home is a puzzle-toy that folds open like a flower. This is the emotional and expository pivot from "courier job" to "save the ward."
locationSlideModel.readAloud: Making your way past the village homes and through the farmland, you find the Custodian's home — though "home" undersells it. A cabin hangs from a braid of rope as thick around as a giant's forearm, tied to a massive branch and counterweighted by a cabin-sized boulder resting at the tree's base. The whole thing sways gently, like overripe fruit ready to drop. The boulder is carved with symbols; the cabin windows flicker with a soft yellow-green light. And the preserve-trees here are different — hundreds of faces carved into their trunks on every side, eyes peering in every direction. What do you do?

gmDetails.title: The Whitefire Custodian (GM-only, canon p.33)
gmDetails.body:
Form: Seven-foot mix of humanoid and firefly; moves in slow-then-suddenly-jerky faerie motions. Face hard to read, but her voice carries all her emotion. Old but spry, mischievous.
Voice sample (canon): "Are you the group Emeris sent from the capital? Oh my, you're rather late, aren't you. Come in, come in."
Manner: Curious about their journey, who directed them to her, and — pointedly — how each of them imagines they might die one day. She notices if a single item in her home is moved an inch.

gmDetails.title: The Package reveal (CANON — read aloud, p.33)
gmDetails.body:
Inside Emeris Crown Holdings' package lies a massive stone with a lion's face carved into it. Marlowe — you recognize this as the Keystone Asset from the capital city's main archway.
The Custodian: "Of course Emeris would keep this delivery secret. If anyone knew your city was no longer warded, you would be conquered before sunrise." Then: "We must travel to the Open Vale Ritual Site to revitalize the ward. Such an effort of magic will attract dangerous creatures from the darkest reaches of the preserve. I'll need your help."

hiddenTruth: GM-only hidden truth: the Custodian may be a true believer being used, a partial witness, or both.
Her fear of the Forgotten Gods should not erase the corporate-sounding texture around the Keystone and ward economy.

title: The Hanging Office Exterior
alt: The Hanging Office Exterior scene art for The Hanging Office.
caption: The Hanging Office is absurd because the system is absurd; the people inside are not.
gmGoal: Run the hanging-home puzzle as a gentle test of patience, courtesy, and cleverness.
publicObjective: Get the Custodian's attention or reach her home.
readAloud: Up close, cabin undersells it. A home hangs from a braid of rope as thick as a giant's forearm, tied to a massive branch and counterweighted by a boulder the size of the cabin itself. The whole thing sways like overripe fruit ready to drop. The boulder is carved with symbols; the windows flash a soft yellow-green light. There is no obvious door at ground level. What do you do?
gmNotes: The goal is not to stump the table. Let the puzzle reveal what kind of guests they are.
Destructive force lowers trust; gentle strength or patient honesty raises it.
gmScript: Say: "This is not a lock to force. It is a person to convince. Call up, climb, study the counterweight, or wait and announce yourselves honestly."
gmReadAloud: A home hangs from a braid of rope as thick as a giant's forearm.
A boulder the size of the cabin counterweights it at the tree's base.
The windows flash with soft yellow-green light.
gmChecklist: Offer all three module options: call, cut the rope, climb.
Cutting the rope blasts them back and costs 1 Stress.
Climbing is Agility 13; failure means a limb gently sets them down.
Clever/courteous solutions nudge custodian_trust up.
festival_boon can help charm or signal her.
gmPrivate: She emerges on something worthy: patience, courtesy, cleverness, restraint, or genuine vulnerability.
Keep consequences whimsical and non-lethal.
playerTakeaway: The way in is to be the kind of people worth opening the door for.
storyTakeaway: The Custodian tests character before access; her home answers courtesy faster than force.
mechanicTakeaway: This is a forgiving puzzle with real cost: call, climb, study, or force it; force costs Stress while cleverness raises custodian_trust.

title: The Whitefire Custodian
alt: The Whitefire Custodian scene art for The Hanging Office.
caption: The Whitefire Custodian is a person, not the adventure's magical help desk.
gmGoal: Deliver the Custodian as the RP heart of Act 4 and let the party earn her trust before the reveal.
publicObjective: Win the Custodian's confidence and hand over the package.
readAloud: The home lowers, and from it steps a being seven feet tall: part humanoid, part firefly, moving in slow drifts broken by sudden jerky motions. Her face is hard to read, but her voice carries every feeling plainly. She eyes your group with open mischief. "Are you the group Emeris sent from the capital? Oh my. You are rather late, are you not? Come in, come in." Inside, the treehouse opens far larger than it should, packed with potion bottles, spellbooks, runes, plants, and small creatures. None of it is messy. You get the sense that if you moved a single item an inch, she would know.
gmNotes: This scene is pure RP with stakes. Dice are optional; trust is not optional.
Per-character hooks belong in perCharacterLayer, not in these notes.
gmScript: Say: "She is warm, weird, ancient, and deciding right now who you are. She rewards honesty and curiosity. Meet her strangeness with warmth and she will meet yours."
gmReadAloud: A seven-foot being steps from the hanging home: part humanoid, part firefly.
Her face is hard to read, but her voice carries every feeling plainly.
Inside, the treehouse opens far larger than it should.
gmChecklist: Describe before naming: seven-foot firefly-faerie first, Whitefire Custodian after she names herself.
Ask about the journey, who sent them, and how they imagine they might die.
Read hush_trust, bramble_truth_learned, strixwolf_blood_debt, and custodian_route.
Set custodian_trust from warmth, honesty, restraint, and answers.
Do not reveal the package truth until S04-04.
gmPrivate: Her knowledge stance is a Kyle canon flag. Play her as warm and guarded; do not resolve whether she fully knows the ward cost.
If strixwolf_blood_debt is true, she can gently name that the forest has been watching the party with teeth.
playerTakeaway: Be genuine with her and she becomes your greatest ally; be cold and she gives only what she must.
storyTakeaway: The person the job served is strange, ancient, warm, and bound to the safety everyone has been circling.
mechanicTakeaway: custodian_trust is the mechanic: warmth, honest answers, restraint, and curiosity decide how much candor and help she gives.

playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The home lowers, and from it steps a being seven feet tall: part humanoid, part firefly, moving in slow drifts broken by sudden jerky motions. Her face is hard to read, but her voice carries every feeling plainly. She eyes your group with open mischief. "Are you the group Emeris sent from the capital? Oh my. You are rather late, are you not? Come in, come in." Inside, the treehouse opens far larger than it should, packed with potion bottles, spellbooks, runes, plants, and small creatures. None of it is messy. You get the sense that if you moved a single item an inch, she would know.

title: The Keystone Reveal
alt: The Keystone Reveal scene art for The Hanging Office.
caption: The Keystone Asset stops being cargo and becomes a communal protection problem.
gmGoal: Route the package reveal through the Custodian, not Marlowe, and set keystone_understanding.
publicObjective: Learn what the package is and what must be done.
readAloud: The Custodian unfolds her home like a blossoming flower and draws the crate inside, sealing it open again as a workshop. She breaks the seal. Inside lies a massive stone carved with a lion's face. She goes still, then nods, slow and grave. "Of course Emeris would keep this delivery quiet," she says. "This is the Keystone Asset: the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward. If the route knew what you carried, every hungry thing in the preserve would follow the scent of it." The light in her home dims as she speaks. "We must take it to the Open Vale and revitalize the ward before Hush has to trust paper promises instead of protection. That much magic will draw dangerous things from the deep preserve. I will need your help."
gmNotes: This is the controlled spoiler release. Earlier player text must not have named the Keystone Asset.
Players can react before choosing prep. Do not rush the table out of shock.
gmScript: Say: "The Custodian carries this reveal. Marlowe can recognize a personal detail if she is present, but the truth does not depend on any one PC."
gmReadAloud: She breaks the seal.
Inside lies a massive stone carved with a lion's face.
"This is the Keystone Asset: the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward."
gmChecklist: Check package_status before starting; if lost, do not run this reveal as written.
Name Keystone Asset here for the first time in player text.
Route recognition through the Custodian.
Marlowe gets only an optional bonus recognition beat.
Set keystone_understanding surface/deep.
Seed, but do not explain, the deeper consume/soul-economy truth.
gmPrivate: If package_status=lost, stop the normal reveal and use only the Kyle-confirmed recovery branch when it exists.
The deepest truth is that the ward protects by consuming. In Act 4 this remains a seed, never a full explanation.
Calibrate her candor to custodian_trust and ward_awareness.
playerTakeaway: The job was never small, and now you know why: you are being asked to finish it at real risk.
storyTakeaway: The package was the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward, and renewing it will draw danger from the deep preserve.
mechanicTakeaway: The reveal writes keystone_understanding: surface from hearing her, deep from Knowledge 14 or hard questions with high trust.

Keystone Asset™: Inside the sealed crate, packed in wax-paper and reassurance, sits a heavy grey stone the size of a loaf, warm to the touch, faintly humming, with a light deep inside it that is slowly going out.
Whitefire Custodian's Ward-Charm: A small hand-carved wooden ratcoon mid-scamper has been thumb-worn smooth for luck. It is warm, and the forest feels a little kinder while you hold it.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.
"The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."
"Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear."
The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.
The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: The job was never small, and now you know why.
player.say: "This is the moment the stakes get honest. Hush safety is in this room, and she is asking you to go further."
player.ask: "React. Ask her what it is, why it was hidden, what the ritual costs, or just take a breath and decide how you feel."
player.deeper: Pause here. Do not push past the reveal until players have had space to react.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The package was the heart-stone for Hush's survival.
story.say: "You were not couriering cargo. You were carrying the thing Hush needs before its protection fails."
story.ask: "Surface truth: it renews Hush's ward, it is dangerous to move openly, and secrecy keeps the route from becoming a feeding trail."
story.deeper: Deeper truth stays gated: it drains or consumes something. Seed only on deep inspection/high trust.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: The reveal writes keystone_understanding.
mechanic.say: "If you want to know more, examine the stone or press her. What you learn shapes how ready you are for what is next."
mechanic.ask: "Knowledge 14: the stone is old, high-tier wardcraft, and draining. Set keystone_understanding=deep. Otherwise set surface."
mechanic.deeper: Marlowe can personalize the recognition, but the Custodian owns the reveal in all cases.

playerSafeProjection.caption: The Keystone Asset stops being cargo and becomes a communal protection problem.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Learn what the package is and what must be done.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The Custodian unfolds her home like a blossoming flower and draws the crate inside, sealing it open again as a workshop. She breaks the seal. Inside lies a massive stone carved with a lion's face. She goes still, then nods, slow and grave. "Of course Emeris would keep this delivery quiet," she says. "This is the Keystone Asset: the heart-stone for Hush's failing ward. If the route knew what you carried, every hungry thing in the preserve would follow the scent of it." The light in her home dims as she speaks. "We must take it to the Open Vale and revitalize the ward before Hush has to trust paper promises instead of protection. That much magic will draw dangerous things from the deep preserve. I will need your help."

sensorySummary: Thin lines run through stone, root, and soil toward the ritual center. Dust lifts from them when the Keystone is near. Some lines are bright where people gather; others are dim near neglected edges.
Ward-light ticks in grooves, wind thins near the center, and voices come back as if the clearing is measuring them.
Ozone, old chalk, wet stone, and a faint sweetness like crushed clover under lightning.
The grooves feel smooth in the center and sharp where the ward has cracked.
Animals keep to the edge. The place feels operational and old, not abandoned.

title: Toward Open Vale
alt: Toward Open Vale scene art for The Hanging Office.
caption: The final approach turns understanding into preparation.
gmGoal: Convert the reveal into commitment, offer real preparation, and bridge to Act 5.
publicObjective: Commit to the ritual and set out for the Open Vale.
readAloud: The Custodian gathers what she needs with the brisk energy of someone much younger than she looks. "The Open Vale is where the ward was first forged," she says. "It is where it must be renewed." She looks at each of you in turn. "I cannot do this alone, and what comes for us when the magic rises will not be gentle. But I think you already knew the job was bigger than a crate." When you are ready, the treehouse unfolds one last time, and the road to the Open Vale opens before you.
gmNotes: This is the bridge scene. The important output is state, not more lore.
A reluctant yes still counts if the party chooses the hard road with eyes open.
gmScript: Say: "Before we go: you can rest, prepare, ask her what to expect, or spend any favor you earned. It all matters when the ritual starts."
gmReadAloud: "The Open Vale is where the ward was first forged."
"I cannot do this alone."
The treehouse unfolds one last time, and the road to the Open Vale opens before you.
gmChecklist: Do not railroad the yes; let the stakes and trust carry it.
Offer prep: rest, learn the ritual, spend festival_boon or Hush favor, plan positions.
Set ritual_prep ready/unready.
Set final custodian_trust.
Set ward_stability fragile/stable for Act 5.
Use MAP-LOC-open-vale-ward-lines as the forward edge.
gmPrivate: Convergence math: high trust + deep understanding + ready prep = ward_stability stable. Otherwise fragile.
If package_status=lost, commitment can exist emotionally but Act 5 cannot proceed normally until the recovery branch is confirmed.

storyScope.antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
storyScope.gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.

act_seeds.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.
"The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."
"Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear."
The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.
The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You are choosing the hard road on purpose.
player.say: "You have signed on for something real. Use this moment: rest, ready up, ask questions."

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The party chooses to finish what the job started.
story.say: "This is the yes. Not for coin, because you have seen enough to care how this ends."
story.ask: "She does not force you. She names the stakes, and your characters decide whether they can walk away."
story.deeper: Let reluctant characters be reluctant. Commitment is stronger when it is not automatic.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway

mechanic.say: "Before we go: rest, prepare, ask what to expect, or spend any favor you earned. It all matters when the ritual starts."
mechanic.ask: "Ready prep eases Act 5. Rushing makes ward_stability fragile and the countdown harsher."
mechanic.deeper: Set ward_stability from convergence: trust, understanding, prep, and boons.

title: Act Five: The Ward Renewal
caption: The finale turns five acts of trust, mercy, preparation, and truth into one visible ritual outcome.
gmGoal: Converge every prior choice into the ward renewal: protect the Custodian, make the countdown legible, resolve the ritual, and choose what truth leaves with the party.
publicObjective: Protect the Custodian through the ritual, renew the ward, and finish what the job started.
readAloud: The carriage pulls into a perfect circle of clearing, the only place in the preserve where the trees pull back and let you see the open sky. This is where it ends. The Custodian says the ward was first forged here, and here it must be renewed. She tells you it nearly killed her the first time. Then she smiles, old and unafraid, and asks you to stand with her while she does the most dangerous thing she knows how to do.

title: The Open Vale Site
alt: Old ritual clearing under open sky.
caption: The quiet before the finale turns care, rest, and preparation into real protection.
gmGoal: Arrive at the old ritual clearing, run the last Short Rest, and turn preparation into finale resources.
publicObjective: Reach the ritual site, learn what is coming, and prepare.
readAloud: The clearing is a perfect circle, the only break in the endless canopy: open sky above for the first time in days. The Custodian speaks softly as you arrive. This is where she first forged the ward pillars that keep Hush safe. She almost died doing it. Then her antennae perk in a disconcerting way. "This is good. Stop, here. Now come help me. I'm old." She begins to glow. "I'll need an hour. Enjoy the night air while you can. We'll be very busy soon."
gmNotes: This is the pressure valve before the finale. Give every player one prep spotlight before moving on.
gmScript: Say: "This is your last calm moment. Short Rest now: Tend to Wounds, Clear Stress, Repair Armor, or Prepare for Hope. Pick two. If you Prepare together, you each get two Hope. I take 1d4 Fear during the rest."
gmReadAloud: The clearing is a perfect circle, the only break in the endless canopy.
The Custodian says this is where she first forged the ward pillars that keep Hush safe.
"I'll need an hour. Enjoy the night air while you can. We'll be very busy soon."
gmChecklist: Deliver the clearing and Custodian history beat.
Run Short Rest: Tend to Wounds, Clear Stress, Repair Armor, Prepare.
Take 1d4 Fear during the rest.
If ritual_prep=ready, let a prepared PC preview the countdown before S05-02.
If package_status=lost, state that the ritual cannot proceed as written until a recovery/improvisation decision is made.
gmPrivate: The Forgotten Gods deflection is canon-facing; do not explain the deeper cost.
The player-facing site is warm Open Vale. Open Vale(TM) registration stays GM-only.
playerTakeaway: This is the quiet before the worst of it; use it well.
storyTakeaway: This clearing is where the ward was born and where it must be renewed, and the Custodian is risking herself again.
mechanicTakeaway: Short Rest is the final resource conversion: HP, Stress, Armor, Hope, ritual_prep, and GM Fear all change the fight.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: This is the quiet before the worst of it; use it well.
player.say: "Last calm moment. Heal up, steady yourselves, and brace. Once she starts, it is all hands."

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: This clearing is where the ward was born and where it must be renewed, and the Custodian is risking herself again.
story.say: "Sacred ground. She made the ward here once, nearly died for it, and she is about to do it again with you to guard her."
story.ask: "If players ask about the Forgotten Gods, she deflects. The deeper cost stays a seed, not an answer."
story.deeper: Keep the moment sincere. Save corporate bite for the report choice.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Short Rest is the final resource conversion: HP, Stress, Armor, Hope, ritual_prep, and GM Fear all change the fight.
mechanic.say: "Short Rest: pick two. Tend to Wounds clears 1d4+1 HP, Clear Stress clears 1d4+1 Stress, Repair Armor restores 1d4+1 slots, Prepare gives Hope; prepare together for two Hope each. I take 1d4 Fear."
mechanic.ask: "If ritual_prep is ready, you know the countdown rules before they hit. If package_status is lost, the ritual cannot proceed as written until we resolve that."
mechanic.deeper: This is the last bookkeeping moment; make it emotional and fast.

playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The clearing is a perfect circle, the only break in the endless canopy: open sky above for the first time in days. The Custodian speaks softly as you arrive. This is where she first forged the ward pillars that keep Hush safe. She almost died doing it. Then her antennae perk in a disconcerting way. "This is good. Stop, here. Now come help me. I'm old." She begins to glow. "I'll need an hour. Enjoy the night air while you can. We'll be very busy soon."

mapData.title: Holding the Line Tactical Map
mapData.caption: A circular clearing with the Custodian and Keystone at the center, skeletons rising close, and wraiths approaching from far range.
sensorySummary: The ritual circle, Custodian, Keystone, skeleton lanes, and wraith edges create a battlefield that points inward.
Bone clicks like old locks, wraith voices flatten into audit language, ward grooves crackle, and the Custodian's breath marks the countdown.
Ozone, cold ash, wet stone, old bone dust, and the antiseptic sharpness of magic trying to price a soul.
Grass stiffens with frost near wraiths; stones buzz under a hand; the center feels warmer only when someone protects it.
The enemies are procedural, but the stakes are communal. Keep returning attention to who and what the ritual protects.
hazards: Clustered skeletons enable Group Attack.
An open center lane exposes the Custodian and ticks the countdown up.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The climax. A perfect circular clearing — the only break in the canopy — where the Custodian first forged Hush's ward pillars. The party takes a Short Rest, then defends her through the ward-renewal ritual against waves of skeletons and Soul-Audit Wraiths while a countdown die ticks. Win condition: survive until the ritual completes, not "kill everything."
locationSlideModel.readAloud: On the Custodian's direction, your carriage rolls into a clearing — a perfect circle, the only patch of the preserve where no trees block the open sky. Stars wheel overhead. This is the Open Vale Site. The Custodian's voice softens as she tells you she forged Hush's ward pillars here, on all four corners of the village — and that she nearly died doing it. She won't say more; something about angering the Forgotten Gods. Then her antennae perk in a way that unsettles you. "This is good. Stop, stop. Yes, here. Now come help me, I'm old." Her body begins to glow, flickering against the dark.

sensoryStack.detail: A flawless circular clearing, open sky (rare here), the Custodian glowing brighter and lifting the carriage a foot off the ground, eyes rolling back; later, skeletons clawing up from the earth and wraiths drifting in from the treeline.
The Custodian humming, then a shriek when the Keystone responds; unearthly screeches from the woods; rusted swords scraping free of the soil.
ozone, turned earth, cold air with no forest-damp — the clearing feels outside the preserve.
Charged, electric; the hair-raising sense of big magic; the open sky disorienting after days under canopy.
The Forgotten-Gods unease; the woods themselves seem to react to the arcane energy.

locationSlideModel.combatBlock:
The ritual countdown (p.35): Set a d8 to 8. Ticks down 1 each time an adversary is defeated; ticks up 1 each time the Custodian is hit. At 0, the ritual completes → Epilogue.
Setup (p.35): Custodian standee center; PCs around her; 4 Legacy Skeletons in Close range of her; 2 Soul-Audit Wraiths in Far range.
Legacy Skeleton — Tier 1 Standard (×4)
Rusted Sword: Melee, 1d6+1 phy · ATK +0 · Difficulty 12 · HP 2 · Stress 1 · Thresholds 7/none
Battle guide: roll d20 (no ATK mod) vs Evasion; hit → 1d6+1. Take 6 or less damage → mark 1 HP; otherwise defeated.
Group Attack (Feature): spend a Fear, move several skeletons into Melee, one shared attack roll at +0; on success deal 4 phy per skeleton, combined into one hit.
Soul-Audit Wraith — Tier 1 Bruiser (×2)
Lifedrain: Far, 2d6+8 mag · ATK +3 · Difficulty 13 · HP 6 · Stress 3 · Major 7 / Severe 14
Spectral Body (Passive): resistance to physical damage (incoming physical halved, round up).
Memory Delve (Action): attack a Close target; on hit, the wraith places a hand on their cheek — ask the player to describe a terrifying childhood moment — then 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest.
Pass-Through (Action): spend a Fear, attack a Melee target; on success the PC is Untethered (can't act until the countdown ticks down). Whole party Untethered at once → all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition cleared.
Open Vale Site — Environment, Tier 1 Exploration
Feature Market Correction (Action): spend a Fear to summon 2 Legacy Skeletons within Very Close of a PC.
GM guidance (p.35): if the countdown stalls, use Market Correction to spawn easy skeletons. If no PC is in range, adversaries target the Custodian (Difficulty 11, narrative damage only). Death move (Quickstart): a PC at last HP falls unconscious until healed or the danger passes — not dead.
transitions: In: From the Treehouse (05), Act Five.
Out: Countdown hits 0 → ritual completes → the Keystone Asset epilogue (see 07 for the sequel hook).
locationSlideModel.canonSource: Countdown rules, all three stat blocks, the environment feature, Short Rest options, and GM guidance are module-canon (pp.34–35).
hiddenTruth: GM-only hidden truth: Soul-Audit Wraiths and Legacy Skeletons read as corporate instruments, not natural spirits.
Run Memory Delve as extraction and the skeletons as repossessed/decommissioned labor logic, while keeping the reveal subtextual.
locationSlideModel.storyTakeaway: Open Vale reveals the ward as living infrastructure under engineered pressure.
locationSlideModel.mechanicTakeaway: The win condition is the ritual countdown reaching 0, not clearing every adversary.

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The climax. A perfect circular clearing — the only break in the canopy — where the Custodian first forged Hush's ward pillars. The party takes a Short Rest, then defends her through the ward-renewal ritual against waves of skeletons and Soul-Audit Wraiths while a countdown die ticks. Win condition: survive until the ritual completes, not "kill everything."
locationSlideModel.readAloud: On the Custodian's direction, your carriage rolls into a clearing — a perfect circle, the only patch of the preserve where no trees block the open sky. Stars wheel overhead. This is the Open Vale Site. The Custodian's voice softens as she tells you she forged Hush's ward pillars here, on all four corners of the village — and that she nearly died doing it. She won't say more; something about angering the Forgotten Gods. Then her antennae perk in a way that unsettles you. "This is good. Stop, stop. Yes, here. Now come help me, I'm old." Her body begins to glow, flickering against the dark.

sensoryStack.detail: A flawless circular clearing, open sky (rare here), the Custodian glowing brighter and lifting the carriage a foot off the ground, eyes rolling back; later, skeletons clawing up from the earth and wraiths drifting in from the treeline.
The Custodian humming, then a shriek when the Keystone responds; unearthly screeches from the woods; rusted swords scraping free of the soil.
ozone, turned earth, cold air with no forest-damp — the clearing feels outside the preserve.
Charged, electric; the hair-raising sense of big magic; the open sky disorienting after days under canopy.
The Forgotten-Gods unease; the woods themselves seem to react to the arcane energy.

The Wraiths' Memory Delve and Pass-Through are your big Fear spends — use Pass-Through sparingly (it can lock a PC out; if the whole party goes Untethered they all mark 2 HP and snap back).

locationSlideModel.combatBlock:
The ritual countdown (p.35): Set a d8 to 8. Ticks down 1 each time an adversary is defeated; ticks up 1 each time the Custodian is hit. At 0, the ritual completes → Epilogue.
Setup (p.35): Custodian standee center; PCs around her; 4 Legacy Skeletons in Close range of her; 2 Soul-Audit Wraiths in Far range.
Legacy Skeleton — Tier 1 Standard (×4)
Rusted Sword: Melee, 1d6+1 phy · ATK +0 · Difficulty 12 · HP 2 · Stress 1 · Thresholds 7/none
Battle guide: roll d20 (no ATK mod) vs Evasion; hit → 1d6+1. Take 6 or less damage → mark 1 HP; otherwise defeated.
Group Attack (Feature): spend a Fear, move several skeletons into Melee, one shared attack roll at +0; on success deal 4 phy per skeleton, combined into one hit.
Soul-Audit Wraith — Tier 1 Bruiser (×2)
Lifedrain: Far, 2d6+8 mag · ATK +3 · Difficulty 13 · HP 6 · Stress 3 · Major 7 / Severe 14
Spectral Body (Passive): resistance to physical damage (incoming physical halved, round up).
Memory Delve (Action): attack a Close target; on hit, the wraith places a hand on their cheek — ask the player to describe a terrifying childhood moment — then 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest.
Pass-Through (Action): spend a Fear, attack a Melee target; on success the PC is Untethered (can't act until the countdown ticks down). Whole party Untethered at once → all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition cleared.
Open Vale Site — Environment, Tier 1 Exploration
Feature Market Correction (Action): spend a Fear to summon 2 Legacy Skeletons within Very Close of a PC.
GM guidance (p.35): if the countdown stalls, use Market Correction to spawn easy skeletons. If no PC is in range, adversaries target the Custodian (Difficulty 11, narrative damage only). Death move (Quickstart): a PC at last HP falls unconscious until healed or the danger passes — not dead.
transitions: In: From the Treehouse (05), Act Five.
Out: Countdown hits 0 → ritual completes → the Keystone Asset epilogue (see 07 for the sequel hook).
locationSlideModel.canonSource: Countdown rules, all three stat blocks, the environment feature, Short Rest options, and GM guidance are module-canon (pp.34–35).
hiddenTruth: GM-only hidden truth: Soul-Audit Wraiths and Legacy Skeletons read as corporate instruments, not natural spirits.
Run Memory Delve as extraction and the skeletons as repossessed/decommissioned labor logic, while keeping the reveal subtextual.
locationSlideModel.storyTakeaway: Open Vale reveals the ward as living infrastructure under engineered pressure.
locationSlideModel.mechanicTakeaway: The win condition is the ritual countdown reaching 0, not clearing every adversary.

title: The Ritual Begins
alt: Short Rest Before the Storm scene art for The Ward Renewal.
caption: The ritual becomes visible pressure: protect the Custodian and drive the countdown to zero.
gmGoal: Start the ritual, show the first threats, and put the countdown die on the table.
publicObjective: Begin the defense and understand the countdown.
readAloud: The Custodian lets out a shrill cry. "The Keystone has finally responded! Surround me, the ritual must begin or I'll lose the pathway! Hurry!" Her glow swells, her eyes roll back, and the carriage lifts a foot off the ground. From the woods comes a chorus of unearthly screeches. The ground rumbles. Rusted swords break the surface as dead things claw their way up. In the distance, two shapes drift toward you, screeching, wrong. Hold the line until she's done.
gmNotes: Market Correction is available as a GM pressure valve, not player-facing terminology.
gmScript: Say: "d8, starting at 8. Defeat an enemy or remove a real pressure, it ticks down one. She gets hit or exposed, it ticks up one. At zero, the ritual is done and you win. The math is simple; staying alive is not."
gmReadAloud: "The Keystone has finally responded! Surround me, the ritual must begin or I'll lose the pathway!"
The carriage lifts a foot off the ground.
Rusted swords break the surface as dead things claw their way up.
Two shapes drift in the distance, screeching, wrong.
gmChecklist: Place Custodian center, PCs around her, 4 rusted-sword skeletons Close, and 2 screeching wraiths Far.
Set ritual_countdown=8.
If ward_stability=stable, soften the first exposure or give a prepared defense a free success beat; if fragile or missing, full canon pressure.
If ritual_prep=ready, let the prepared PC explain the countdown in character.
Initialize protected_whom as unresolved and start watching who covers whom.
gmPrivate: Use description before names: rusted-sword dead, floating screeching wraiths. Names and deeper meaning can come after the table understands what they see.
playerTakeaway: This is the fight that ends the story: keep her safe and run the clock down.
storyTakeaway: The ritual is live and irreversible now; the only way out is through.
mechanicTakeaway: The countdown die is the win condition: d8 starts at 8, down on enemy defeat or pressure removed, up when the Custodian is hit.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
official_results.success_with_hope: Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: The rest becomes bookkeeping instead of care before danger. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: Soul-Quiet Charm, Firstmoss Poultice.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

rollCards.hope_spin: Gain Hope. Let the Hope result make the scene more generous, clear, or player-directed when it fits the fiction.
rollCards.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. Add pressure, reveal cost, spotlight a threat, or advance a visible consequence.
gm_fear_spends: Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.
class_community_ancestry_reveals: Ask who helps someone else without making a big deal of it.
rollCards.duality_text: Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add the chosen trait, compare to the Difficulty, then read the higher die for Hope/Fear spin.

playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The Custodian lets out a shrill cry. "The Keystone has finally responded! Surround me, the ritual must begin or I'll lose the pathway! Hurry!" Her glow swells, her eyes roll back, and the carriage lifts a foot off the ground. From the woods comes a chorus of unearthly screeches. The ground rumbles. Rusted swords break the surface as dead things claw their way up. In the distance, two shapes drift toward you, screeching, wrong. Hold the line until she's done.

title: Holding the Line
alt: The Ritual Begins scene art for The Ward Renewal.
caption: Holding the line teaches that defeating pressure and protecting the center are the same victory.
gmGoal: Run the rusted-sword skeleton wave as clear protection pressure and countdown progress.
publicObjective: Defeat the rusted dead and keep the Custodian safe.
readAloud: The skeletons come in a clatter of rust and bone: not clever, but endless, and all of them reaching for the glowing figure at the center. For every one you put down, the ritual's clock ticks a notch closer to done. But they keep clawing up out of the dirt, and the Custodian cannot defend herself. The line is yours to hold.
gmNotes: Skeletons are pressure and countdown fuel, not a slog. Keep them moving toward the Custodian.
gmScript: Say: "They are not strong. They are persistent, and they want her, not you. Stand in the way. Every one you drop moves the countdown down by one."
gmReadAloud: The skeletons come in a clatter of rust and bone.

The line is yours to hold.

abilities: Spectral Body - Passive: resistance to physical damage; halve incoming physical damage and round up.

fear_moves: Pass-Through - spend Fear, Melee attack: on hit, the PC becomes Untethered and cannot act until the countdown ticks down.

block5.combat_summary: Tier 1 Bruiser; Diff 13; thresholds 7/14; HP 6; Stress 3; ATK +3; Lifedrain, Far, 2d6+8 magic
block5.person_under_the_fight: Once a debt collector who took the job to save their own family from the ledger, and then could not stop collecting. The medallion was an employee badge; the name is scraped away so thoroughly that only the balance is still legible. Protection freely given, or a memory offered without a price, makes the shape flicker like it half-remembers being owed to someone too.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: Hold the perimeter; every skeleton you drop is a step toward the end.
player.say: "Cut them down, keep them off her, watch the clock fall. This part you can win with grit."
player.ask: "Position between the dead and the Custodian, strike the nearest, and call out if they start to swarm."
player.deeper: Keep the first combat wave empowering before the wraiths complicate it.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The first wave is beatable, but it never stops reaching for her.
story.say: "They are not strong; they are persistent, and they want her, not you."
story.ask: "Describe them as rusted-sword dead first. If players ask later, the GM term is Legacy Skeletons."
story.deeper: The corporate-asset undertone stays GM-side unless earned.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Skeleton defeats tick the countdown down, but Group Attack spikes damage if the party lets them cluster.
mechanic.say: "Squishy alone. Hit one hard enough and it is gone; clock ticks down. Let them cluster and I can spend Fear for one ugly combined hit."
mechanic.ask: "Difficulty 12, HP 2, 1d6+1 physical. Group Attack is one +0 roll, 4 physical per skeleton combined."
mechanic.deeper: Use Group Attack as warning/payoff for ignored clusters, not surprise punishment.

title: The Soul-Audit Wraiths
alt: Legacy Security Skeletons scene art for The Ward Renewal.
caption: The wraiths make care and grounding as important as attacks.
gmGoal: Escalate into wraith pressure where memory, vulnerability, and rescue become the emotional core.
publicObjective: Survive the wraiths, protect each other, and keep the ritual on track.
readAloud: The drifting things reach you, and they do not swing for your body. One presses a cold hand to a face and reaches inside, dredging up something buried. The other simply passes through a body like a door, and for a horrible moment a soul stands outside itself, unable to move, unable to act, while the fight roars on without them. These are worse than the dead. These ask questions you do not want to answer.
gmNotes: Use Pass-Through sparingly. Rescue and grounding should return players to action quickly.
gmScript: Say: "These do not want your blood. They want your worst memory and your soul out of your body. If someone gets knocked loose, protecting and calling them back is the scene."
gmReadAloud: The drifting things reach you.
They do not swing for your body.
A cold hand reaches inside memory.
A soul can stand outside itself for one horrible moment.
gmChecklist: Use Soul-Audit Wraith stats: Difficulty 13, HP 6, Stress 3, ATK +3, Lifedrain Far 2d6+8 magic.
Physical resistance halves incoming physical damage, round up.
Memory Delve: Close attack; ask for a terrifying childhood moment, then 3d4+9 magic and Vulnerable until next rest.
Pass-Through: spend Fear, Melee attack; on hit target is Untethered until countdown ticks down.
Whole party Untethered at once: all mark 2 HP, souls return, condition clears.
Track protected_whom as the primary emotional write.
gmPrivate: Memory Delve hooks live in perCharacterLayer. Use the active PC's hook if helpful, but accept any player-safe version.
Soul-economy stays a seed. The word itself is GM-only.
playerTakeaway: You cannot out-muscle these; protect each other, cover the Untethered, and endure.
storyTakeaway: The wraiths attack who you are, not just what you can take.
mechanicTakeaway: Memory Delve, Vulnerable, Pass-Through, Untethered, and grounding an ally make care a live combat mechanic.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Soul-Audit Wraiths
playerSafeProjection.alt: Legacy Security Skeletons scene art for The Ward Renewal.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The wraiths make care and grounding as important as attacks.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Survive the wraiths, protect each other, and keep the ritual on track.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The drifting things reach you, and they do not swing for your body. One presses a cold hand to a face and reaches inside, dredging up something buried. The other simply passes through a body like a door, and for a horrible moment a soul stands outside itself, unable to move, unable to act, while the fight roars on without them. These are worse than the dead. These ask questions you do not want to answer.

title: The Peak
alt: Soul-Audit Wraiths scene art for The Ward Renewal.
caption: The peak asks what the party saves when it cannot save everything cleanly.
gmGoal: Run the peak HOLD/BREAK choice and let resource spends, protection, and sacrifice decide the outcome track.
publicObjective: Survive the peak and drive the countdown home.
readAloud: It all comes at once: the dead clawing up faster, the wraiths pressing in, the Custodian's glow guttering like a candle in wind. The clock is close, but so is disaster. Every choice now costs something: guard her and leave a friend exposed, or save the friend and let her take the hit that sets you all back. There is no clean way through. There is only what you are willing to give.
gmNotes: No PC is required to land the final blow. Let any meaningful action create the final tick if fiction supports it.
gmScript: Say: "All-in time. Spend Hope, boons, big abilities, tag-team moments, and last good ideas. You cannot cover it all, so what you choose to save becomes the ending."
gmReadAloud: It all comes at once.
The Custodian's glow gutters like a candle in wind.
The clock is close, but so is disaster.
gmChecklist: Threaten the Custodian honestly.
Offer Death Move choices heroically if a PC marks their last HP: Blaze of Glory, Avoid Death, or Risk It All.
Use HOLD if she is protected and the party drives the countdown home cleanly.
Use BREAK if someone falls, she is hit badly, or the win is bought with a severe cost.
Seed ritual_outcome as clean, costly, or pyrrhic; finalize protected_whom.
gmPrivate: Custodian death remains a Kyle canon flag. Use dying only as a marked unresolved possibility unless ruled live.
playerTakeaway: This is the moment you will remember: give everything, choose who you save, and finish it.
storyTakeaway: You cannot save everything, so what you choose to save becomes the ending.
mechanicTakeaway: Peak play spends Hope, boons, tag-team actions, Death Moves, and final countdown ticks to write ritual_outcome and protected_whom.

A contract can move a package. It cannot decide what a life is worth.
If you are here to help, stand where help costs you something.
block2.secrets: The ward's cost is personal, and the deepest economy behind that cost is worse than she will say unless trust and understanding are earned.
block2.fears: The stone waking hungry, the Relay failing, and being remembered as infrastructure instead of a person.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: This is the moment you will remember: give everything, choose who you save, and finish it.
player.say: "Whatever you have been saving, now. Decide who you stand in front of and bring the clock home."

story.statement: You cannot save everything, so what you choose to save becomes the ending.

story.deeper: HOLD/BREAK should be visible and emotionally fair.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: Peak play spends Hope, boons, tag-team actions, Death Moves, and final countdown ticks to write ritual_outcome and protected_whom.

mechanic.ask: "Every Custodian hit is +1; every defeat or true pressure removal is -1. Near the end, one choice can change clean to costly or costly to pyrrhic."
mechanic.deeper: No single PC owns the final tick. Any meaningful action can close the ritual if earned.

title: The Ward Renewed
alt: Ward renewal light over the ritual clearing.
caption: The ward renews, the field goes quiet, and the cost finally becomes visible.
gmGoal: Resolve countdown zero, clear the field, and set ritual_outcome and custodian_fate.
publicObjective: Finish the ritual; the ward is renewed.
readAloud: As you land the blow that drops the last threat, the ritual ends. The carriage crashes back to earth and the Keystone blazes with arcane light. Then a soundless explosion erupts from the Custodian, washing outward, dissolving any enemy still standing. The screeching stops. The clawing stops. The clearing is quiet again, the open sky calm above you. It is done. The ward is renewed. You held the line, and a city you may never see will wake tomorrow still safe.
gmNotes: If custodian_fate=dying, mark it as a canon-sensitive result until Kyle rules whether she can die.
gmScript: Say: "Clock at zero. Fight over. The blast clears whatever remains. You do not have to mop up. Breathe, then we count what it cost."
gmReadAloud: The carriage crashes back to earth.
The Keystone blazes with arcane light.
A soundless explosion washes outward.
The clearing is quiet again.
gmChecklist: End combat immediately when ritual_countdown reaches 0.
Clear remaining enemies with the ritual release.
Set ritual_outcome=clean, costly, or pyrrhic from S05-05.
Set custodian_fate=well, drained, or dying if Kyle/table canon allows.
Give a quiet breath before S05-07.
gmPrivate: The win is real. The cost is felt. Soul-economy stays dread, not exposition.
playerTakeaway: You held long enough. It is over, and the ward is renewed.
storyTakeaway: The city is safe tomorrow because the party held the line tonight.
mechanicTakeaway: At countdown zero, combat ends immediately; ritual_outcome and custodian_fate carry the cost into the denouement.

abilities: Spectral Body - Passive: resistance to physical damage; halve incoming physical damage and round up.
Memory Delve - Action, Close attack: on hit, the player describes a terrifying childhood memory, then takes 3d4+9 magic and becomes Vulnerable until next rest.
Grounding response: Presence or Knowledge 13 can call back an Untethered ally when the fiction supports it.
fear_abilities: Pass-Through - spend Fear, Melee attack: on hit, the PC becomes Untethered and cannot act until the countdown ticks down.
Whole party Untethered at once: all mark 2 HP, souls return, and the condition clears.
gm_ready_notes: Use Memory Delve on one player at a time; keep everyone else engaged with rescue, cover, or grounding actions.

Let the behavior imply soul-economy dread; do not explain the hidden thesis unless earned later.

block5.combat_summary: Tier 1 Bruiser; Diff 13; thresholds 7/14; HP 6; Stress 3; ATK +3; Lifedrain, Far, 2d6+8 magic
block5.person_under_the_fight: Once a debt collector who took the job to save their own family from the ledger, and then could not stop collecting. The medallion was an employee badge; the name is scraped away so thoroughly that only the balance is still legible. Protection freely given, or a memory offered without a price, makes the shape flicker like it half-remembers being owed to someone too.
block5.combat_lever: Ritual completion, memory refusal, or destruction of the audit form ends the threat.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You held long enough. It is over, and the ward is renewed.
player.say: "You made it. The line held. Breathe; the worst is behind you."
player.ask: "Check on each other. The immediate threat is gone; recovery happens in the denouement."
player.deeper: Let relief land. Do not rush straight into paperwork.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The city is safe tomorrow because the party held the line tonight.
story.say: "A city you may never see wakes tomorrow still safe because you held this clearing tonight."
story.ask: "The enemies are gone. The Keystone is charged. What it cost stays felt rather than explained."
story.deeper: This is sincere victory with a shadow.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: At countdown zero, combat ends immediately; ritual_outcome and custodian_fate carry the cost into the denouement.
mechanic.say: "Clock at zero. Fight over. Blast clears the field. Now I set ritual_outcome and custodian_fate from what happened."
mechanic.ask: "Clean means strong relief, costly means visible strain, pyrrhic means severe price. Dying Custodian stays canon-sensitive until Kyle rules."
mechanic.deeper: Carry the exact state into S05-07.

title: Beyond the Contract
alt: The Ward Locks Into Place scene art for The Ward Renewal.
caption: The adventure ends with what truth the party chooses to carry forward.
gmGoal: Honor the finale, run the report choice, and bridge to the Epilogue through report_choice.
publicObjective: Wrap your story, decide how you report what happened, and learn what comes next.
readAloud: An hour later, back in the treehouse, the Keystone hangs suspended over a rumbling hearth-fire. The Custodian, older now, exhaustion plain in her voice, folds herself into an over-stuffed chair. "You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone." She lets you sit with it, the warmth and the weight both. And then, because there is always one more thing: she has a question about what you will tell the people who sent you, and a map to somewhere the light is going wrong.
gmNotes: The report choice is the satirical gut-punch: real heroism meets paperwork and future liability.
gmScript: Say: "The fight is won. Now the real question: what do you put in the report? File honest, spin corporate, refuse to report, or withhold the truth. That choice decides the Epilogue tone."
gmReadAloud: The Keystone hangs over a rumbling hearth-fire.
The Custodian looks older now.
"You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone."
She asks what you will tell the people who sent you.
gmChecklist: Name protected_whom and honor the PC or group that covered the worst moment.
Name ritual_outcome and custodian_fate in the denouement tone.
Gate deeper truth: only keystone_understanding=deep + custodian_trust=high gets the strongest dread hint.
Offer report_choice: file-honest, spin-corporate, refuse, withhold-the-truth.
Set relay_hook_accepted if the party takes the Goldspire Relay hook.
Bridge S05-07 -> S06-* by report_choice.
gmPrivate: Truth-hint ladder low: the form has boxes for cost, blame, and recoverable asset, but no box for who was protected.
Truth-hint ladder medium: the Custodian flinches when lives, memories, or warmth are described as resources.

Truth-hint ladder high: only if keystone_understanding=deep and custodian_trust=high, say the frightening part is not that wards need power, but that someone learned how to profit from what protection consumes.
Do not fully explain soul-economy. Let players reach for the conclusion.
playerTakeaway: You saved a city. Now decide what story you tell about it, and whether you answer the next call.
storyTakeaway: The adventure ends not with the fight, but with who gets to own the truth of what happened.
mechanicTakeaway: report_choice gates the Epilogue, while ritual_outcome, protected_whom, custodian_fate, and relay_hook_accepted carry the finale forward.

rollCards.why_this_trait: Knowledge supports the craft; Presence steadies the people tied to it.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
official_results.success_with_hope: Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

outcomes.hard_failure: The ward returns unstable or emotionally hollow. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
outcomes.near_miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: Ward Renewal Chime.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

official_results.critical_success: Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.

official_results.success_with_fear: Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.

outcomes.hard_failure: The system edits the victory before anyone else hears it. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.

outcomes.mixed_success: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
outcomes.strong_success: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
outcomes.exceptional_success: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: Lion-Sealed Writ.
outcomes.critical_success: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

player.title: Player takeaway
player.statement: You saved a city. Now decide what story you tell about it, and whether you answer the next call.
player.say: "Heroes do not get a clean ending here; they get a form to fill out. What do you write? And do you take the next job?"
player.ask: "Say goodbye to the Custodian, ask what you have been holding, choose the report, and decide whether the Relay hook stays open."
player.deeper: Let players talk. This is the final agency beat.

story.title: Story takeaway
story.statement: The adventure ends not with the fight, but with who gets to own the truth of what happened.
story.say: "The fight is won. Now the real question is what story leaves this clearing, and who that story protects."
story.ask: "If they understand the cost, the report is moral pressure. If they do not, it is still how they frame a job well done."
story.deeper: Report choice is the story thesis; do not reduce it to bookkeeping.

mechanic.title: Mechanic takeaway
mechanic.statement: report_choice gates the Epilogue, while ritual_outcome, protected_whom, custodian_fate, and relay_hook_accepted carry the finale forward.
mechanic.say: "Set report_choice now: file-honest, spin-corporate, refuse, or withhold-the-truth. Then set whether they accept the Relay hook."
mechanic.ask: "file-honest risks retaliation, spin-corporate buys safety with complicity, refuse breaks the frame, withhold-the-truth has the largest future fallout."
mechanic.deeper: Exact long-tail branch consequences remain Kyle-adjudicated; the options are implemented as GM-selectable state now.

title: Back in the Hanging Office
alt: Back in the Hanging Office scene art for Beyond the Contract.
caption: Back at the Hanging Office, the party can see how the contract changed them.
gmGoal: The Keystone rests above the hearth while the Custodian thanks the party.
publicObjective: Rest, receive your due, and reckon with the choice you made.
readAloud: An hour later, back in the treehouse, the Keystone hangs suspended above a rumbling hearth-fire, glowing soft and settled. The Custodian, older now, the night's work plain in her voice, folds into an over-stuffed chair. "You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone." There is hot food, a warm bath waiting, and for the first time in days, nowhere you need to be. She looks at each of you like she is memorizing you. "Before you go," she says, "let's talk about what happened out there, and what you'll do with it."
gmNotes: Use triumphant, bittersweet, pyrrhic, or tragic tone from ritual_outcome and custodian_fate.
If package_status=lost somehow reached here, frame this as an alternate close and flag the normal reward text as changed.
gmScript: Say: "This is the good part. The fire, the food, the old faerie who is alive because of you. Level up, collect what you earned, and let the report choice sit in the room."
gmReadAloud: The Keystone hangs suspended above a rumbling hearth-fire.
The Custodian looks older, exhausted, and deeply grateful.
"Before you go," she says, "let's talk about what happened out there, and what you'll do with it."
gmChecklist: Grant level-up.
Distribute pay, goodwill, and the Custodian's parting gift.
Name protected_whom and ritual_outcome in plain emotional language.
Deliver report_choice payoff: honest, spin, refuse, or withhold.
Set rewards_granted and epilogue_tone.
Drop only one hidden seed if the table asks the right question.
gmPrivate: Reward first. The hidden thesis has not earned space until the players feel the win.
If custodian_trust is high, the Custodian can almost say: the ward does not make safety from nothing. Stop there.
Do not explain the soul-cost. Let it remain a seed.
playerTakeaway: You are heroes tonight: take the reward, take the level, and take the moment with the person you saved.
storyTakeaway: You saved something real, and the person you saved wants to thank you.
mechanicTakeaway: Level-up, rewards_granted, epilogue_tone, and report_choice payoff resolve the one-shot's consequences.

playerSafeProjection.readAloud: An hour later, back in the treehouse, the Keystone hangs suspended above a rumbling hearth-fire, glowing soft and settled. The Custodian, older now, the night's work plain in her voice, folds into an over-stuffed chair. "You fought hard. I'm not surprised. Emeris doesn't send just anyone." There is hot food, a warm bath waiting, and for the first time in days, nowhere you need to be. She looks at each of you like she is memorizing you. "Before you go," she says, "let's talk about what happened out there, and what you'll do with it."

title: The Relay Spire Hook
alt: The Relay Spire Hook scene art for Beyond the Contract.
caption: The Relay Spire hook points beyond the one-shot without stealing this ending.
gmGoal: The Custodian reveals another relay spire may be failing.
publicObjective: Learn what is stirring west, and decide whether you leave that door open.
readAloud: The Custodian leads you out of the treehouse, out of the forest itself, to look down on the green expanse from above. Twisting stone spires break through the treeline, each with a flame flickering in its tower like a beacon. "There's a relay out west," she says, "maybe a few hours. You might have felt it on the way in: its light was weaker than it should be. I think something's wrong with its Keeper, and I fear what happens if that fire goes out." She studies the horizon. "When you're ready, come back. I'll give you my map, so you can make it there safe. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."
gmNotes: The Relay is seen and described, not entered.
If epilogue_tone is pyrrhic or tragic, the hook feels like unfinished business rather than excitement.
gmScript: Say: "One more thing on the horizon. Not tonight unless you want it tonight: a fire going dim, a Keeper in trouble, and a map waiting if you ever come back."
gmReadAloud: Twisting stone spires break through the treeline, each with a flame flickering like a beacon.
"There's a relay out west," she says. "Its light was weaker than it should be."
"When you're ready, come back. I'll give you my map."
gmChecklist: Deliver official Relay hook player-facing.
Offer the map as a future door, not a forced next scene.
Drop 0-4 hidden hints only if earned and the players bite.
Let players say the conclusion; do not lecture.
Set relay_hook_accepted, hidden_hook_discovered, and sequel_direction.
End open-ended. No combat, no countdown, no next act transition.
gmPrivate: Hidden thesis: the corporation manufactures the peril it profits from protecting against.
The official hook and hidden hook point to the same future destination, but the table only gets the hidden conclusion if they articulate it.

Hint ladder: convenient Relay failure; the Custodian almost saying safety is not made from nothing; Bramble truth if learned; staged attack/defensive monster/trademarked havens/assets pattern if they connect it.
Hold the soul-economy as a seed. Do not explain the mechanism.
playerTakeaway: You can rest easy tonight, and if you want, a door west is open.
storyTakeaway: The night's won, but a distant light is failing and the party may be the kind of people who answer.
mechanicTakeaway: relay_hook_accepted, hidden_hook_discovered, and sequel_direction record which ending door the table leaves open.

playerSafeProjection.title: The Relay Spire Hook
playerSafeProjection.alt: The Relay Spire Hook scene art for Beyond the Contract.
playerSafeProjection.caption: The Relay Spire hook points beyond the one-shot without stealing this ending.
playerSafeProjection.publicObjective: Learn what is stirring west, and decide whether you leave that door open.
playerSafeProjection.readAloud: The Custodian leads you out of the treehouse, out of the forest itself, to look down on the green expanse from above. Twisting stone spires break through the treeline, each with a flame flickering in its tower like a beacon. "There's a relay out west," she says, "maybe a few hours. You might have felt it on the way in: its light was weaker than it should be. I think something's wrong with its Keeper, and I fear what happens if that fire goes out." She studies the horizon. "When you're ready, come back. I'll give you my map, so you can make it there safe. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."

locationSlideModel.readAloud: We pull out of the Custodian's home, out of the forest itself, to see the verdant expanse from above — and there, breaking through the treeline, twisting stone spires, each with a flame flickering inside it like a beacon. The Custodian's voice follows you up: "There's a Goldspire Relay, just west of here. You may have felt it on the way to the ritual — its power was strange. The light felt weaker than it should be. I think something might be terribly wrong with the Relay Keeper, and I fear what will happen if its fire is extinguished altogether. When you're ready, come back, and I'll give you my map so you can make it there safely. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."

locationSlideModel.gmOrientation: The closer. After the ritual, back in the treehouse, the Custodian thanks the party and plants the next adventure: a Goldspire Relay spire to the west whose beacon-flame is weakening, with something wrong about its Relay Keeper. This is denouement + sequel bait, not a playable location yet. Keep it evocative and unresolved.
locationSlideModel.readAloud: We pull out of the Custodian's home, out of the forest itself, to see the verdant expanse from above — and there, breaking through the treeline, twisting stone spires, each with a flame flickering inside it like a beacon. The Custodian's voice follows you up: "There's a Goldspire Relay, just west of here. You may have felt it on the way to the ritual — its power was strange. The light felt weaker than it should be. I think something might be terribly wrong with the Relay Keeper, and I fear what will happen if its fire is extinguished altogether. When you're ready, come back, and I'll give you my map so you can make it there safely. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."

I'll need to watch it carefully to ensure nothing cracks or becomes sentient or anything of the like. You know how it is." Then she asks the party for one more thing — pointing them at the Relay.

entities.name: The Titan's Steps
entities.summary: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.
entities.role: Make vertical logistics feel lived in, not decorative.
entities.personality: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.; introduce it with a sensory palette, who feels safe there, and what has been neglected.
entities.wants: Pull player attention toward the choices, clues, and relationships tied to The Sable Sinecure, Helena Corain, Mountain Crabs.
entities.sampleLine: A colossal pillar route rising more than a thousand feet through Sablewood, where merchants pay for altitude in sweat, rope, and hazard rate.

entities.name: Mountain Crabs
entities.summary: Granite-shelled cliff crabs with moss and alpine flowers growing on their backs, stone-heavy claws, many gripping legs, and wary eyes made for vertical roads.
entities.role: Crab-shell resource and climbing-route pressure
entities.personality: Grumpy granite tenants of the cliff with gardens growing on their own backs. Not malicious, just enormous and territorial on a road where one bad step is the last. They were here long before the climbing route and resent the traffic.
entities.wants: To be left to the cliff and the moss on their shells, and to keep the warm crevices they have always nested in.
entities.sampleLine: A deep grinding click you feel in the stone before you hear it.

entities.name: Fire-Falcons
entities.summary: Sleek ember-orange falcons with coal-black wing tips and feather edges like banked fire, beautiful enough for prestige and sharp enough to make a cache feel watched.
entities.role: Violent light-bearing Sable Sinecure companion birds
entities.personality: Beauty bred into a weapon. Banked-fire feathers the wealthy buy for spectacle and the Sinecure trains for harm. Loyal to whoever feeds them, sharp to everyone else, and aware, somewhere, that they are admired far more than they are loved.
entities.wants: To hunt, to be fed by a steady hand, and to keep the high perch they have claimed.
entities.sampleLine: A bright scaling shriek that turns every head across a market.

entities.name: Sableblade
entities.summary: Growing straight up out of dark forest soil, like a sapling that decided to be a sword, is a blade of living dark wood and pale metal. It has no maker's mark and hums when your hand nears the hilt.
entities.role: Sableblade: an ancient Sablewood weapon. Agility melee, one-handed, d10+1 physical; mark Stress before damage to add +3 damage.
entities.personality: A stress-fueled weapon rumored to grow from the forest during one of Sablewood's seasonal expansions.; use Sableblade as a concrete table object with texture, ownership, and a reason it matters now.
entities.wants: Give players a tangible handle on Sablewood™ Logistics Preserve, Forgotten Gods, Sablewood Hope Moments, whether they inspect, carry, return, trade, or refuse it.
entities.sampleLine: A stress-fueled weapon rumored to grow from the forest during one of Sablewood's seasonal expansions.

entities.name: Eeligator Scale Shield
entities.summary: A round shield of overlapping slick green-grey scales catches the light like river-water. It smells of deep water, mud, and old teeth.
entities.role: Eeligator Scale Shield: sharp-scaled river armor. Add +1 to damage thresholds and +2 to damage rolls.

entities.personality: Seamless armor made of polished stones cut like scales so Union folk can move through barbed thickets.; use Bramble Union Stoneweave as a concrete table object with texture, ownership, and a reason it matters now.

entities.name: The Glimpse
entities.summary: A half-seen deer-wolf apparition made of moonlit mist, thin branches, too many reflective eyes, and firefly motes that make mercy feel older than fear.
